items.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
items.summary:
OpenAI
November 2, 2026
Engineering
Scaling Git at OpenAI
Building agentic-scale source control while investing in the Git ecosystem.
By Aaron Friel, Taylor Blau, and Ted Nyman, Members of Technical Staff
Over the past year, the size and demands on our monorepo have increased at a staggering pace. It was clear that we needed to revamp our source control system to scale to the level of concurrent work that Codex makes possible.
We built Pando, a new backend for Git repositories, without interrupting any engineering work or changing how our team uses Git. Pando now powers all development in OpenAI’s monorepo. Pando is designed to meet two ambitious goals: first, horizontally scalable writes, optimized for concurrent pushes to many branches. And second, maximize read throughput, so clients can download data fast enough to fully saturate their available network bandwidth.
We met these goals while retaining compatibility with the Git protocol and client, enabling both our engineers and agents to seamlessly adopt Pando into their existing workflows. In production, Pando cut median push latency by nearly 5x. It now delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day.
Here, we’ll cover our motivations for building a new source-control system, along with why we chose to retain compatibility with Git. We’ll compare our system with common approaches to scaling Git, describing why Pando is uniquely capable of meeting OpenAI’s scalability needs. We also discuss what’s next, and how we’ll continue contributing to Git to support agent-scale work.
Why we needed a new source control system
Codex has changed the scale and pace of development at OpenAI, enabling engineers to do far more work in parallel. That means more branches and pushes, more merges, and more fetches and clones from development environments, research jobs, and CI.
These demands compound. One engineer now has several changes ready for CI at once, and each push can set several jobs fetching the same commit.
Starting around the end of last year, the systems supporting our monorepo were struggling to keep up. We suffered slow fetches and pushes along with failed merges, with reliability at times falling below 90%. Had we reached a limit of Git itself, or of the way we served our monorepo? Git grew out of a community that exchanged patches to the kernel via email. For more than two decades, developers have adapted their tools around Git as the way they build software has changed. When we started to feel friction in our own monorepo, it mattered to us that we could keep building on that work.
We saw a way to keep that familiar workflow while rebuilding the backend to handle pushes to different branches in parallel and serve the same history to many readers concurrently. Building on Git as the foundation of our source-control workflow meant that improvements to the client could be useful beyond OpenAI. We wanted to contribute those improvements from our copy of Git⁠(opens in a new window) to upstream, sharing them with the broader community.
Engineering for Git at scale
Scaling a source control system has two essential dimensions: many writers pushing to different branches, and many readers fetching the same history. Pando optimizes for both.
First, Pando coordinates updates to each branch independently. Updates to unrelated branches can proceed in parallel, and a reader fetching a branch gets the history needed for that revision. The tradeoff is that a reader looking at several branches can see them at different points of time.
Second, Pando reuses packfiles (Git’s format for compressing multiple objects together) across fetches instead of generating an individual packfile for each client. A client may download some objects it already has, but the server can serve the same bytes to many clients with little computation.
These choices let us scale writes across branches and serve reads from caches. To see how they fit together, let’s start with how Git stores and transfers history.
Git object storage primer
Git must be able to keep two parts of a repository in sync: objects and references.
A Git repository records snapshots of files and the history connecting them as a graph of objects. An object may be either a blob, tree, commit, or tag. Blobs hold the content of an individual file, and trees associate names with blobs or other trees to form a directory structure. Commits point to a root tree and zero or more parent commits, forming the history of your repository.
Objects are identified by a hash of their type and contents. Objects are also immutable: recording a changed file creates a new blob, while unchanged files and directories can reuse existing objects.
Branches and tags are references, or “refs”, that point to commits. Committing on a branch creates a new commit and updates the branch’s ref to point to it.
Git objects reference each other by their ID, commits to trees, and trees to trees and blobs. The branch refs/heads/main points to commit C2, whose parent is C1. C1 points to root tree T1, where parser.py refers to blob B1. C2 points to root tree T2, where parser.py refers to blob B2. In both root trees, docs/ refers to the same tree, T3. Its README.md entry points to blob B3, and usage.md points to blob B4.
Git stores objects in either a “loose” or “packed” state. Loose objects are stored in individual files identified by their object ID. Packed objects are stored together in a packfile, enabling similar objects to be stored as deltas against one another.
Git can store blobs as separate files or pack them together, encoding one blob as a delta against another.
In Git, an object is reachable from a commit if Git can find it by following links from that commit through its parents, trees, and blobs. During a fetch, the client tells the server which commits it wants and which it already has. The server finds the objects reachable from the wanted commits, excludes those it knows the client already has, and sends the remainder as a packfile in the same format Git uses on disk. A full clone starts without any objects, so it needs all the objects reachable from the history being cloned.
A push transfers objects in the other direction by asking the server to update one or more refs. The client uses the server’s set of advertised refs to avoid sending objects the server already has. The pack being sent can therefore depend on existing objects: receiving the pack alone is not enough to reconstruct the new history.
Replicating a Git repository means keeping both objects and references available across multiple servers. Before a replica can serve a reference’s new value, it must be able to supply the objects reachable from that value. The service also needs to coordinate competing reference updates, i.e., pushes that try to move the same branch from the same old tip to different new commits. Systems that impose a single order on all writes to a repository can make pushes to unrelated branches wait on one another.
Existing distributed Git service patterns
While designing Pando, we evaluated conventional approaches for scaling source control using Git: one that coordinates ref updates across repository replicas using three-phase commit (3PC, a protocol for coordinating a commit across multiple nodes), and one that orders updates through a shared write-ahead log (WAL, a record of changes written before they’re applied) in blob storage.
Three-phase commit (3PC)
In the three-phase commit design we modeled, the Git service keeps a complete copy of the repository on several replicas. When any server receives a push, the incoming packfile is copied and sent to all replicas in parallel. To publish the push, a majority of replicas must accept the ref update. The server managing this is the coordinator, and it requires multiple rounds of communication between the coordinator and each other replica.
To accept a reference update, each replica locks its copy of the ref and checks that it still points to the commit the client expects. The coordinator then sends a pre-commit message to the replicas that accept. Once a majority acknowledges the pre-commit message, the coordinator tells them to perform the update. Any up-to-date replica can then advertise the new branch tip from its local copy of the repository.
Keeping complete replicas makes it possible to serve reads locally, and guarantees that clients get a consistent view of all references no matter which replica they pick. As a consequence, references are updated one at a time, and each push requires multiple round trips to coordinate the ref update among replicas.
Waiting for a quorum puts replica disk performance and communication latency on the push path. As write volume grows, the replicas must keep up with incoming packs as well as read traffic.
Write-ahead log (WAL)
In the WAL-based design we modeled, the Git service uses a shared manifest in blob storage to order updates across the repository. When a server receives a push, it uploads the incoming packfile to a blob store and prepares the ref update in its local copy of the repository. To publish the push, it adds an entry to a shared manifest stored in the blob store that records the ref update and points to the packfile. The Git server then updates the manifest using a compare-and-swap operation. This atomically replaces the manifest, or otherwise rejects the change. If another writer has updated it in the meantime, the server reads the intervening entries, checks that its ref update is still valid, and retries using the packfile it already uploaded.
Writers can upload their packfiles in parallel, but even pushes to unrelated branches require updating the same manifest. The round-trip time for a successful compare-and-swap limits how often the repository can publish a new manifest. A low-latency blob store makes this step fast. Batching lets one manifest update several refs at the same time, at the cost of queueing updates and increasing latency.
The blob store can receive packfiles in parallel, but updates to the shared manifest still compete with one another. Increasing the blob store’s capacity alone doesn’t resolve that bottleneck. Each replica still needs to read and index packs from the blob store before it can serve them locally. If incoming writes outpace that work, replicas fall behind and clients wait longer to fetch newly pushed commits.
Architecting Pando
That brings us to Pando. Pando is a new architecture for serving Git repositories with the goal of scaling to many clients pushing simultaneously. Here’s how it works:
Rethinking constraints
Prior to developing Pando, we had a hunch that we could meet our requirements without compromising on Git, but we did need to compromise on some of the things that most Git systems assume to be requirements:
Repository-wide consistency: Providing a consistent, point-in-time snapshot of all refs requires coordination across the repository. In a system that orders all ref updates together, pushes to unrelated branches contend on a single coordination point.
Unique packfiles for every client: If two clients with different local histories fetch the same branch, the server may need to generate a different pack for each to avoid sending objects they already have. Creating these responses costs CPU and disk I/O, making it difficult to scale to high volumes of readers.
Instead, Pando provides a relaxed consistency model (causal consistency) to scale writes, and reuses packfiles to scale reads.
Causal consistency (CC)
When a client pushes to a branch, Pando stores the incoming packfile as an immutable blob in a blob store. Each time the branch moves, Pando records a ref version containing the new tip, the pack that supplied it, and any earlier ref versions the pack depends on in a metadata store. Both the blob store and metadata store are horizontally scalable.
Fetching a commit or reference from Pando requires replaying a set of ref versions (packfiles) to the client, reconstructing the state of the client that created the ref version being fetched. This provides a weaker form of consistency across the entire repository, while providing serializability for updates to individual refs. Clients only conflict when pushing to the same ref simultaneously. A client reading several branches cannot assume those reads describe a single point in time across the repository.
A push to trunk adds an incremental pack, containing one or more commits. Each push to a side branch includes the topic’s earlier commits again, so a client with the advertised trunk version can fetch the topic in one pack.
This is a form of causal consistency. In order to fetch a reference, the reader observes the history of the writer that produced it. During a push, Pando controls what shared history the client and server agree on, ensuring clients produce more easily shared packfiles.
As a consequence, Pando doesn’t provide a point-in-time state of all references during Git operations or an ordering of ref updates within a clone or fetch. Concretely, suppose that branches foo and bar are both updated during the negotiation of a full clone. During the negotiation, one client may observe foo at version 1 and bar at version 2, while another client observes foo at version 2 and bar at version 1. In practice, users and agents are agnostic to the global ordering of ref updates, and instead depend on the order of updates to a single reference.
Comparing Approaches
In this simulation of the three consistency models we configure 1,000 clients to each select a distinct branch and then repeatedly push unique commits, measuring total wall clock duration and push to fetch latency. The latter is an important metric for workloads, as it measures round trip time for users and agents to collaborate or to use other systems which rely on version control. The simulation models hardware ranging from commodity to premium virtual machines and blob storage systems. In this simulation, we’ve relaxed repository-wide consistency for three-phase commit.

The modeled three-phase commit system shows significantly greater write latency under load as their disks saturate; meanwhile, write-ahead log systems show significantly greater read latency for the same reason, as servers struggle to keep up with reading from the journal. In both real world testing on our monorepo and in this simulation, Pando supports many thousands of clients able to push concurrently without impacting performance under load.
On handling a push, Pando validates the incoming packfile while streaming it to blob storage, without unpacking it into a local repository. When a client begins a fetch Pando selects the stored packs the reader needs, and the reader downloads them. No server needs to apply packfiles to a local repository or perform costly unpack and packing operations. Because these servers primarily perform negotiation and packfile selection, Pando servers can run on commodity hardware.
This allows Pando to scale to the limits of clients, the network between clients and Pando, and the blob storage service. With enough capacity, clients working on independent branches can each transfer packs as fast as their own connection allows. To serve more clients at that rate, we can add Pando servers and scale the metadata store and blob store alongside them.
Pushing and Fetching a Branch in Pando
Pando stores the writer’s packfile in blob storage and records the ref version in metadata service. On fetch, Pando selects the packs the reader needs, and Express serves them.

Packfile URIs
An agent edits files and creates a commit locally and runs git push, which creates a packfile of those changes to update a branch. Pando receives the pack and streams it to blob storage. After validating the incoming push with a single pass decode, Pando uses a multi-key transaction to record a ref version in our metadata store and atomically update the ref pointer. This enables Pando to provide “read-your-own-write” consistency. This entire write operation requires O(1)O(1)O(1) metadata reads and writes.
When another client fetches the branch, Pando selects a set of stored packs using the history the client already has. This operation requires O(log⁡Δ)O(\log \Delta)O(logΔ) metadata reads, Δ\DeltaΔ being the shortest distance in ref versions between what the client has and what the client wants. The server returns packfile URIs, and the client downloads them through a service, Express, that stores packfiles in regional caches.
This design relies on the three central services of Pando’s architecture: pushes, fetches, and compaction.
Scaling pushes
When a client pushes, a conventional Git server is like a poker player showing all of its cards, revealing to the client every branch it has. The client then gathers the commits, trees, and blobs to create a packfile that excludes objects it knows the server already has.
Advertising more refs can make the push smaller. It can also make the pack harder to reuse, because another client may be missing objects the writer left out.
Pando takes a different approach. Instead of showing its full hand, it only advertises a select set of branches to the client. This is done for two reasons:
Providing a consistent view of every ref is expensive. With millions of branches, the ref advertisement alone can exceed 100 MiB. Providing this requires each server to either maintain a current mapping, requiring significant coordination overhead, or a database query that scales with the number of refs.
By providing only a subset of the refs to the client, the client will generate a pack that depends only on what the server explicitly allows the client to exclude. Tracking the dependencies allows Pando to reuse the packfile a client generates in one push by serving it as the response to a subsequent fetch.
As a Git server advertises more refs, clients pushing have more sources from which to exclude objects, enabling them to produce smaller packs. However, reusing these packfiles requires the server to be able to prove the clients fetching have each of the dependencies. Otherwise, the packfile may omit objects the client needs.
On the other hand, if a Git server advertises none at all, the client would generate a packfile containing the repository’s full history. That packfile can be used by any other client, but at the significant cost of making fetching any branch effectively a full clone.
Advertising more refs results in smaller packfiles. Most of the size reduction can come from advertising just one.
By default, when a client pushes a new feature branch, Pando advertises only a designated trunk branch as a base. This keeps the advertisement the same size as the repository gains branches, but comes with tradeoffs. When an engineer either pushes to a single branch many times, or stacks one feature branch on top of another the client has to resend everything outside of the trunk.
This causes successive branch pushes to be larger, containing potentially-redundant objects, and uses additional client bandwidth. In our monorepo, the median packfile produced this way was under 20 KiB, and the 99th percentile was under 3 MiB. For us, this was a sensible trade-off because a reader that already has the advertised trunk history can fetch the branch with that one packfile.
After choosing the set of refs to advertise to the client, Pando accepts the push and updates its metadata store. Pando splits the metadata update into synchronous and asynchronous portions. The synchronous metadata update ensures clients can immediately fetch the newly updated commit. This writes a new ref version and updates the ref pointer mapping to that new version storing that new tip, the dependencies used to negotiate the packfile, and a link to the packfile that was pushed.
At the same time, asynchronous work is recorded in the same transaction, such as scheduling compaction. For very large pushes, only a subset of commits are written synchronously. This allows us to require only a constant number of reads and writes to the metadata store, regardless of the size of the push.
Importantly, Pando servers can accept pushes to unrelated refs independently. The only contended key is the ref pointer, which we guard using an atomic compare-and-swap-like operation. We can scale up write throughput by adding Pando servers, metadata store scaling units, or blob stores.
Line-rate fetch and clone performance
When a client performs a fetch, it provides the server with two sets of commit IDs, known in the protocol as haves and wants. In a conventional Git server, the server computes the set difference among the objects reachable by the haves and those reachable by the wants, compresses them, and sends the result to the client. While the open-source Git server has a variety of indexes locally to accelerate this operation, these packfiles can be expensive to compute and are generally resistant to caching.
Instead, Pando uses the commit mappings recorded on pushes to look up the client’s haves and wants, resolving them to a set of ref versions that contain those commits. Each of those ref versions links to a packfile previously received by Pando. The server uses this to solve for what the client needs, selecting the packfiles that cover the set of objects the client needs.
Planning fetches in Pando
Pando compares what a client has with what it wants, then selects the stored packfiles needed—including any missing branch dependencies.
Branch ABranch BHAVE4WANT31Already heldFetchMissing branch dependency

Pando maps the Git protocol’s haves and wants to a sequence of ref versions. Wanting a side branch implies wanting up to its dependencies on the trunk.
The Git protocol only allows a single packfile to be sent in the HTTP response on a clone or fetch. However, an under-appreciated feature of the Git protocol, packfile-uri, allows a server to return links to download additional packs separately. Pando uses this exclusively, and transmits an empty packfile inline. To support this feature, OpenAI contributed a number of improvements to packfile-uri upstream.
OpenAI systems operate in many geographic regions, so we maintain Pando clusters with local caches in each. A pack delivery service, Express, caches our blob store, and a separate service caches the metadata store. These caches enable Pando to serve requests for a commit ID or a special read of a ref entirely from the cached state in that cluster. We use consistent hashing to route requests for a packfile to Express servers, with cache hit rates of over 99%.
This system of caches provides extremely high throughput, capable of saturating the network limit between clients and Pando. Using these packfile URIs and local caches, we’ve validated that using only standard cloud provider virtual machines, we see clone and fetch operations saturate 10 Gbps network links.
Compaction and time to first byte
For most Git servers, repacking and garbage collection are necessary to maintain the performance of a growing repository. Both of these steps reclaim space, but are compute- and I/O-intensive.
In a fast-moving repository like OpenAI’s monorepo, it is infeasible to send an individual packfile URI for every push that has occurred since the last fetch. Each day, a client would need to download tens of thousands of packfiles to catch up their trunk.
Instead, Pando combines packs in the background to reduce this overhead, adopting a design similar to compaction in log-structured merge-trees. Each push produces what Pando refers to as an “L0” packfile, representing the smallest unit of data Pando can transmit. Over time, background workers collect these packfiles into covers spanning a sequence of ref versions, scaling geometrically from L0. Today, our monorepo uses up to L4 packfile covers.
These covers serve a dual purpose. After a cover is sufficiently full, a compaction worker will claim it and produce a single packfile. This improves the compression ratio by reorganizing the objects inside the packfile. But it also improves fetch negotiation performance by acting as skip list over ref versions. By scanning through indexes at each level simultaneously, Pando can select a set of packs to send to a client in logarithmic time. These packfile covers, repacked or not, enable a more efficient solution to fetch planning, reducing both throughput and latency requirements for Pando.
Compaction in Pando
Small packfiles are grouped into larger covers across levels, improving compression and speeding up fetches.
PlayPublish a cover over existing packsL2L1L0Compaction in progressPublished cover
Compaction combines packfiles from many ref versions in the background, enabling more efficient fetches with fewer files.
Unlike many Git servers, packfiles are kept at every level and not discarded or garbage collected. Packs at every level are used to serve clients continuously, based on the haves and wants they request in a fetch. And for clients using Pando as an API, reading an arbitrary object from a packfile tends to require reading less data from an L0 than an L4, because it’s less likely to be compressed.
Compaction in Pando significantly reduces both the total transfer size sent to clients and enables pack planning to scale sub-linearly in how far behind the client is. This is especially important for large and quickly changing repositories, which we expect to be a new normal in software development.
Building Pando
We built Pando with Codex, moving from kick-off to production, in just 10 weeks. The core of Pando was designed by a single engineer, implemented by teams of agents, and deployed by a handful of engineers. Pando began serving production traffic in April of this year, and is one part of a larger system of source control management tools used at OpenAI.
We employed a wide variety of approaches when validating Pando’s design. We applied our principles for building more secure software foundations⁠. As a greenfield project, we chose to implement Pando in Rust and without legacy dependencies. We wrote a conformance test suite so agents could test their changes against standard Git behavior. We also developed deterministic simulation testing harnesses allowing us to check invariants and properties of the system, enabling us to find and mitigate subtle race conditions and regressions in negotiation and pack planning.
Many models contributed to this system; as new models became available, we used them to improve Pando’s performance and reliability. Using GPT‑6 Astra, agents wrote Lean and TLA+ to formalize a “theory of Pando” that we used to find and fix bugs in the implementation, and prove properties of the system. Multiple continuous sessions ran for hundreds of hours finding and fixing edge cases in Pando. We also run agents around the clock to red-team Git and Pando using Daybreak-capable models.
Deploying Pando
Our initial deployment of Pando was as a read- and write-through proxy to our existing source control system. This allowed us to keep Pando and the previous system in sync, so we could safely move traffic onto Pando without downtime.
As part of its caching design, Pando can also deduplicate and combine requests before proxying. This allowed us to keep our existing tools healthy as we moved systems to Pando one at a time. As we migrated more workloads to Pando, their pushes populated Pando’s cache and improved the reliability of our previous backend.
In order to optimize performance when using Pando, we began shipping our public distribution of Git to developer machines and within the ChatGPT desktop app. To migrate clients to Pando, we used an internal wrapper around the Git CLI to migrate clients in phases. We created many other tools for handling change requests, code review, and APIs for automations. We migrated hundreds of integrations that depended on legacy APIs, webhooks, and repository downloads alongside Git traffic.
Codex itself helped developers and teams make the move. We created skills for preparing existing checkouts, and for guiding agents to use the new system. As a result, developers could simply ask Codex to migrate their development environments and services.
Switching to Pando improved merge reliability and reduced the latency of the median push by nearly 80%.
Pando can deliver a petabyte of Git data per day with just a handful of CPU cores. Pando has served more than 57 terabytes of Git packs in a single hour, with more than 99% of those bytes from local disk cache.
Reusing packs lets many clients download the same repository history with little computation on the serving nodes. This example shows a single repository, but Pando is designed to support many more. As demand grows, we can scale data delivery and Git negotiation independently.
Contributing back to the Git project
Building Pando on the Git protocol and client helped us identify bugs and opportunities to improve Git’s own performance.
For example, Pando serves reusable packs directly to clients, so downloading and indexing those packs became a central part of making the system fast and reliable. That work surfaced edge cases in concurrent downloads, cleanup after interrupted transfers, and resuming downloads that had already completed. We fixed those paths, added validations when accepting an existing pack for a fetch, and contributed that work back upstream.
We also needed to see where time and bandwidth were going, so we added tracing for packfile-uri downloads and byte counts for pack generation, making it easier to tell whether a slow fetch was spending its time generating packs or transferring them.
In OpenAI’s Git build⁠(opens in a new window), the client can download and index independent packs in parallel. We added the concept of “explicit haves” so a server can advertise a branch’s current tip separately from the history a pushing client may leave out of its pack. On Pando, this enables clients to use --force-with-lease to check that a feature branch hasn’t moved and build its pack against trunk alone. Anyone with that trunk history can then fetch the branch using the same pack.
Several of these improvements are already in upstream Git, and many others in our public repository. We’re continuing to work with the Git community to make these improvements useful beyond Pando. You can follow that work in our public patch tracker⁠(opens in a new window).
What’s next
By rethinking conventional wisdom on how to scale Git repositories, Pando enables us to scale our monorepo without changing the Git workflows our engineers and agents already use. In our monorepo, Pando has unlocked a greater degree of parallelism, improved merge reliability, and reduced the time it takes to publish code changes. Beyond our monorepo, we’re also exploring other uses for Pando within OpenAI, including workloads where large numbers of agents need to collaborate on a shared Git repository.
As engineers and agents produce more software, more teams beyond OpenAI will encounter the limits we hit in source control. We’re currently exploring ways to share the technology that makes Pando possible with our users.
Pando builds on two decades of experience from users and operators of Git repositories. We’ll continue to develop Pando while working with the open-source Git community to share any improvements that benefit Git users more broadly.

In October, we released new AI tools to help you work, stay safe, and learn. We introduced Gemini 4 Argon for complex tasks, Genie 4 for building interactive simulations, and updated Android to block sophisticated scams. You can also use our new SynthID Detector to verify if content is AI-generated. These updates aim to make technology more helpful for your daily projects, personal security, and creative hobbies.
Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.
For more than 20 years, we’ve invested in machine learning and AI research, tools, and infrastructure to build products that make everyday life better for more people. Teams across Google are working on ways to unlock AI’s benefits in fields as wide-ranging as healthcare, crisis response, and education. To keep you posted on our progress, we're doing a regular roundup of Google's most recent AI news.
Here’s a look back at some of our AI announcements from October.
October underscored our commitment to AI innovation, as we released one frontier model globally and announced our next one just two weeks later. After rolling out Gemini 4 Argon — a frontier reasoning model — to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers, we announced Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model yet for long-horizon engineering and cybersecurity defense. Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward while strengthening our safety guardrails in tandem. Elsewhere in October, we introduced Genie 4 for real-time interactive world simulation with native audio, unveiled our smartest fitness tracker with Google Fitbit Edge, broke open a 20-year bottleneck in quantum computing, and more.
Put Gemini 4 Argon to work today, and see what’s next for Gemini 4 at the frontier. Following early safety testing, Gemini 4 Argon rolled out globally for complex coding, financial analysis, and legal workflows across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Google Cloud, Search, and the Gemini app, while also powering physical-world reasoning through Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics. Showing how quickly we’re pushing the frontier forward, two weeks later we announced Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model yet with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. Just as we did with Argon, we’re taking a deliberate approach to rollout: Carbon is now in pre-release testing with the U.S. government and a subset of trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program as we refine safety guardrails and expand partner testing ahead of a broader launch to developers, businesses, and consumers.
Step into real-time interactive worlds with Genie 4. Genie 4 brings unprecedented realism, advanced physics, lifelike human movement, and native audio to real-time interactive simulation. You can steer scenes as they unfold using natural language. Genie 4 advances on our ability to create safe training environments for robots and AI agents as a crucial step toward AGI. Explore the demos on the Google DeepMind blog.
Verify AI-generated content more easily around the world. Having already watermarked more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio with SynthID, we’re expanding SynthID Detector globally in English so anyone can check whether an image, video, or audio clip was generated with AI. Alongside built-in verification tools in Search, Chrome, and the Gemini app that regularly handle over a million requests each day, SynthID Detector also identifies AI content from industry partners like OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao, and Apple.
Stay protected from mobile scams with new Android safeguards. AI-powered Scam Detection in Phone by Google and Google Messages already flags more than 5 million suspected scam calls and texts every month. Now, Android is introducing an opt-in Enhanced protection mode in Google Messages that uses Private AI Compute and our latest cloud Gemini models to catch sophisticated conversational scams, paired with expanded chat alerts and stronger call-forwarding and screen-sharing defenses.

How can I tell if content is AI-generated?
You can determine if content is AI-generated by using the SynthID Detector, which is being expanded globally in English to allow users to check whether an image, video, or audio clip was generated with AI. Additionally, built-in verification tools are available within Search, Chrome, and the Gemini app to assist with identifying AI content.

Meet Google Fitbit Edge, our all-new smartest fitness tracker ever. Available now in a slim, comfortable design with up to seven days of battery life

.
See how AI could improve patient-physician relationships in clinical care. In Google’s first publication in the main journal of The Lancet, researchers from Google and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center evaluated our AMIE conversational medical AI system during real-world primary care clinic visits. By gathering patient histories and generating clinical summaries before urgent care appointments, AMIE helped clinicians prepare in 75% of cases and matched doctors’ final differential diagnoses 90% of the time. This is part of our broader work applying AI to better understand, detect, and treat disease.
Create and play custom games in Playground. Our new experimental gaming platform lets anyone build, remix, and share custom single- and multiplayer games from simple text prompts with zero coding required. That same no-code creativity is expanding across our platforms: Android users can now build personal AI apps with Google AI Studio and install them directly on their phones through Google Play, and music producers can vibe code custom instruments and audio plugins in Google Flow Music.
Celebrate educators and sharpen your learning. For World Teachers’ Day, teachers from around the globe shared how they use Gemini to personalize lessons and spark critical thinking, alongside a new global idea search launched in partnership with TED. Whether you’re in the classroom or preparing for a big project, you can also study smarter with Gemini Notebook using interactive learning overviews and custom quizzes, and use new co-creation controls to shape your Slide Decks and Video Overviews before they generate.
Discover more
How can these new updates help students?
According to the article, students can study smarter by using Gemini Notebook, which provides interactive learning overviews and custom quizzes. Additionally, students can use new co-creation controls to shape their Slide Decks and Video Overviews before they are generated.
This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.
Build privacy-first multimodal search with EmbeddingGemma 2. Engineered on the Gemma 4 architecture with 740 million parameters, our new open embedding model moves beyond text to map code, images, video, and audio into a single unified space right on everyday devices. Its modular design cuts local vector storage by up to 6x, making it easy for developers to build private, offline apps that can find a specific video clip from a voice memo or search hours of audio with a text query.
Read the first AI response beamed back from our Project Suncatcher satellite. After launching TPUs into low-Earth orbit, our first Project Suncatcher prototype satellite returned the first-ever AI response generated by a data center-class Google TPU in space: a haiku composed onboard by Gemma 4. This milestone confirms our hardware survived launch and can run AI workloads in orbit. Our team will continue to test how the chips handle radiation and thermal extremes while harnessing space’s abundant solar energy as part of a long-term moonshot toward scalable orbital AI infrastructure.
See how our latest research is accelerating scientific discovery. At our annual Research@ 2026 event, we shared new ways we’re putting advanced AI in the hands of scientists and experts — including demonstrating an experimental Geospatial Reasoning agent, opening public access to our Deep Review tool for technical papers, and delivering top-ranked flu hospitalization forecasting. These breakthroughs are part of a broader, company-wide effort to push the boundaries of scientific discovery. Beyond the event, Google teams are also advancing planetary research by mapping the world’s forest types, while Google.org has awarded $36 million to 17 organizations accelerating scientific breakthroughs with AI.
See how we broke open a 20-year bottleneck in quantum computing. In a landmark study published in Science, Google Quantum AI demonstrated that a technique called "magic state cultivation" works in practice on our Willow quantum processor, cutting errors roughly 40-fold compared to uncultivated states. Because producing high-purity magic states previously threatened to consume up to 95% of a quantum computer’s resources, this breakthrough clears a major hurdle on the path to large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers.
Discover more
I am a tech expert. What does this month's news mean for me?
For a tech expert, these October 2026 updates represent significant advancements in model capabilities, development tools, and hardware infrastructure. Key takeaways include the release of Gemini 4 Argon for complex coding and financial workflows, and the announcement of Gemini 4 Carbon, a model specialized in long-horizon engineering and cybersecurity defense. Developers can now build personal AI apps via Google AI Studio for direct installation on Android, utilize EmbeddingGemma 2 for privacy-first, offline multimodal search on edge devices, and experiment with Genie 4 for real-time interactive world simulation. Furthermore, the successful deployment of a data center-class TPU in orbit via Project Suncatcher and the breakthrough in "magic state cultivation" on the Willow quantum processor signal major progress in specialized hardware and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

items.title: 个性化视频技术：历时七年的算法演进
items.summary: 原创 抖音用户体验算法 2026-11-02 19:03 北京 01 | 前言 个性化视频算法是抖音体验算法团队在行业内最早创设的方向，曾于 24 年发表详述，参考： 首度揭示！个性化视频技术——短视频体验的秘密！ (https://juejin.cn/post/7439556806602752051) Personalized Playback Technology: How Short Video Services Create Excellent User Experience(https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17073) 数年以来，团队笃行不怠，多路并进，与当时披露的内容相比又有更多进展，在此做一详细盘点，希望可以引导、促进业界水平的提升。 回顾历史，音视频技术自互联网开端时即已成为显学，在之前三十多年的发展历程中，行业的关注重点主要在编解码标准、流媒体协议和框架开发等方向，虽然一直有零散的算法工作，意图解决实际工作流程中某一环节的问题，但抖音这条路径是通过 VLP、UIAE、Reward、CDNPilot、TACO、Demand、Vision、PRIME 等一系列算法将整条音视频链路串联起来建模，构建出完整、精细，同时又真实的个性化视频技术体系。 需要说明的是，抖音在基础视频消费之外，还承载了包括商业化、直播、电商、生活服务、短剧、游戏、搜索等数十种不同业务，需要在更高的性能资源占用约束下，追求流畅度、画质、稳定性、失败率、成本等方向的综合最优，对其中的算法技术而言，就需要其个性化算法涉及的规模和精度，与他人做法拉开跨代、量级上的差距，才能保证市场竞争优势。 与相对“传统”的音视频工作相比，个性化视频技术同时追求算法的实际价值、创新度与复杂度，因此在常规的优化武库之外，会将视野投向包括大型推荐模型、强化学习、控制论、因果推断、运筹优化、认知科学等在内所有具备潜在可能的技术，令其与音视频技术结合，交融并汇，才有希望达成“具备跨代、量级差距”的效果。 02 | 服务端：从单点规则到系统运筹 2.1 视频价值预测：VLP VLP（Video Lifecycle Prediction）是大型短视频服务需要回答的一个基础问题：每个视频（预期）到底值多少钱？这个值将决定转码资源的分配优先级、CDN 缓存策略和分发权重，甚至影响前处理流程、内容理解的推理预算。每天抖音有几千万到上亿条视频上传，传播与消费价值差异巨大，需要模型对每条视频的未来价值（vv、播放时长）做出预测，才能更精确地决定在后续链路上如何处理与干预。 抖音或其他短视频 App 的生产-消费模式，均处于一种基尼系数极高的情况，极少的视频投稿就可以覆盖多半以上的视频播放，而由于大量对视频的处理——例如转码、前处理、内容理解——十分昂贵，在满足基础服务及内容安全要求的前提下，提高大规模视频处理系统的整体效率成其为必然。 本质上，虽与 Ranking 或 CTR 问题有别，VLP 面对的仍是一种高精度的预测问题，适合用与推荐、商业化等领域相近的解法，因此有参考许多字节内外推荐团队的工作，未来的思路也会尽力与推荐、计算广告等领域的前沿工作对齐，吸纳其在建模、模型结构、特征运用、样本分析等方面的进展，并针对音视频领域调整。 VLP v1（2021） 让视频价值第一次在音视频链路中高精度地被计算出来，此前业务只能按粉丝数、历史播放vv做规则排序——也是业界的习惯做法，一些视频服务曾构建过预测服务但精度甚低，VLP v1 搭建了完整类推荐的召回、排序链路，引入数十个作者、视频特征，用排序模型把价值预估变为监督学习，将输出归一化到 0~1 的热度分供转码排序使用。VLP v3（2023）第一次使用超大规模稀疏 DNN 并支持天级更新，稀疏特征经 Embedding 拼接后送入多层前馈网络，用 LHUC 方式依据作者/类目表征生成取值 [0, 2] 的逐层缩放向量做个性化调制，以 BIAS 让关键特征直连输出层（wide & deep 思想），同时从「单一价值分」升级为多任务，一个模型同时预测未来 1d/3h 的 vv、完播、播放时长等目标，并用 GradNorm 自适应平衡各任务损失： （往左滑动查看完整公式） VLP v8（2026） 深度实践了 LRM scaling-up 路线，进一步推动了个性化推荐、计算广告与音视频领域的技术交叉，v7 的人工特征交叉（MMCN 等）结构复杂且天花板低，self-attention 加深后 token 表征趋同（cosine相似度 0.9+，即 over-smoothing），v8 在广泛尝试对比了不同推荐技术进展的效果后，选择字节推荐团队的 TokenMixer 结构堆叠替代特征交叉主干，用 PerTokens AFFN为FFN 引入 token 级自适应门控，剪枝冗余结构后将 dense 参数扩至 1B，可验证视频价值模型同样服从scaling law（Reg-AUC 较 v7 +1.36%，MFU +167%），其核心结构与规模规律可概括为： （往左滑动查看完整公式） 图1：VLP v8 的 TokenMixer 主干、Adaptive-FFN 与 Mixup 结构 配合模型复杂度提升，v8 在特征侧同步做了大幅度扩展，新增了数十个 LLM 挖掘特征（视频互动水平、投稿信息、作者生态等），基于视频内容理解大模型生产的 124 个高阶语义特征（音视频画质、美学、结构、热度分析、...），接入多模态 Embedding 和投稿侧序列特征等。此外，拆分了 CAPP（Content and Creator Profile-Aware Popularity Prediction）模型作为 0vv 冷启动场景的补充，专门解决新视频在无历史数据时的流行度预测问题。 2.2 档位组合决策：UIAE 档位组合解决「给每个视频转几个版本、每个版本什么规格」的问题，由于视频压缩基本不可瞬时完成的特性，对同一源片提前准备多个码率/档位视频给不同用户（或同用户的不同访问时段）消费，以求取更高的用户体验，是行业惯例。 与 Content Aware Encoding 内容感知编码受到「传统」音视频算法工程师的关注不同，由我司参考 Brightcove 公司Context Aware Encoding 概念所开创的档位组合（UIAE 及其前序技术）方案视野更投向链路乃至业务的整体最优，首次令服务端与客户端的音视频链路得以形式化的方式串联到一起，将优化目标与终极目标重新塑造一致并统筹优化，是个性化视频领域的基石技术之一。个性化视频技术追求全链路精确可计算、全链路最优化，UIAE 的发展将视频处理与用户未来动态的选择进行链接，支持精确预测与在线运筹，指向全链路的理论上限。 UIAE（User-Item Aware Encoding）前序使用的方案主要采用离线预计算出的固定档位组合，在不同国家和地区均曾取得良好收益，而 UIAE 的思路是，根据用户播放行为和视频编码特性，实时地动态输出可变组合，同时把决策粒度从「群体统计」推进到「用户×视频」，在转码成本约束下最大化个体期望体验： （往左滑动查看完整公式） 参考：A User-Item Aware Encoding Framework for Short Video（https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11461328） UIAE v1（2024） 把前序方案的固定组合改为模型预测的可变组合，将问题建模为带约束的最优化，以各档位的播放概率 p(R) 对体验加权求期望，在码率区间、相邻档位码率差、档位数量与 CRF 等约束下选出期望 QoE 最高的一组档位，简化来看，QoE 可视为画质、卡顿、首帧三项 QoS 的组合，当视频价值上升触发「加转」时会触发重新计算： （往左滑动查看完整公式） UIAE v2（2025） v2 补回了 v1 中被简化的变量，沿「系统拆分+场景细分+自适应」的方向精细化，先按不同系统分别预估 QoS/QoE，把播放环境按不同选档策略细分统计概率，使用 Convex Hull 在 RD 曲线上筛出高性价比候选 CRF 点、枚举生成候选组合集合，再让不同编码器基于各自线上 Context 联合决策。QoE 则改进为 mVMAF（VMAF 的均值变体）、码率、卡顿时长的组合，超参数随场景与人群差异化（如 iOS 画质权重高于 Android），最终取期望体验最大的组合并辅以规则微调： （往左滑动查看完整公式） UIAE v3（2026） 沿同一决策框架扩展，新增 864p 等多个非常规候选档位，并调整多个现有档位超参，同时把转码决策与多码率下发策略联合优化——将设备能力、高峰 / 非高峰时段、大包 / 小包等下发规则纳入约束与统计场景（如低端机过滤高码率档、窄屏低清处理等），即目标函数不变，但在候选空间与可行域上大幅提升： （往左滑动查看完整公式） 2.3 转码资源调度：Reward Reward 算法回答大规模音视频链路中另一个未曾充分建模的问题：有限的转码资源如何分配给海量视频？抖音每日亿级投稿量下，转码集群容量始终有限，Reward 将问题看作资源约束下的收益最大化问题，从召回的 { 视频，档位 } 候选中选择子集提交转码，使总收益最大。 Reward 算法与 VLP、UIAE 统一下载决策：Demand 下载算法所希望回答的问题是，在用户还没划到下一个视频之前，应该提前下载哪些数据、下载多少？下载得少，滑到即卡顿，下载得多，用户划走后未播放的数据即成为纯粹的带宽浪费——在巨大的流量规模下，任何一点冗余都会被放大，其难点在于，决策必须在观看行为发生之前做出，因而本质是一个「以观看概率为权重、在体验收益与带宽成本之间取平衡」的预测与调度问题。 随着内容生态从纯短视频扩展到中长视频、直播与短剧，决策粒度也并不意外地从单视频、固定 Size 逐步细化到播放列表级、按秒与下载 Range 级。 音视频链路算法化的难点始终在建模上。作为前AI时代与互联网伴生发展的若干最复杂的技术领域之一，它很早就被「古法」程序员们使用各种抽象组合式、控制论式、复杂系统式的方法搭建了似简实繁的工程技术栈（播放器、流媒体服务），同时其实际工作时又依托于复杂、极具噪声的网络环境背景，此外，由于决策的频次极重，对性能损耗的容忍与一般的端智能模型相比有数量级的差异。因此每次建模和决策方式的提升尝试，背后的主要工作将是如何克制地运用算力、引入先验知识并克服偏置，「驯服」基本的变量，推动对应的工程改造，使其在复杂系统之中并不带来额外损失，且得到所需的计算性质。 短视频最早策略化的部分是预加载，常用的是固定策略，于当前视频下载完成后预加载后续 N 个视频、每个视频提前加载数百 KB，在抖音这些参数均由海量实验筛选得出，它在短视频为主的阶段十分有效，打败了大量看似精巧的算法方案，但稍长的视频引入后，还是会带来命中率低、数据浪费、卡顿上涨等问题。 早期抖音还采用过一种名为水位阀的技术，引入安全水位 S 与危险水位 D 双阈值闸门，当前缓冲水位高于 S 时开闸，将后续视频预加载任务串行插入当前视频 Range 请求间隙，低于 D 时关闸保播放，同期还结合了端智能快慢滑预测的能力来调整预加载大小。 Dynamic v1（2022） 在水位阀基础上引入动态水位机制与预加载Ladder设计，从有限个固定大小任务变为多任务配置组合，基于网速、卡顿、播放进度、快慢滑标签等多维信号动态调整阈值、预加载个数与大小，对抖音的用户活跃度有明显正向影响，带宽成本也有较大下降。 Dynamic v2（2023） 有三项演进：一是引入Weibull 观播时长建模，用形状k、尺度λ、位置μ三参数描述CDF，支持服务端离线多维画像（片源/用户/视频）与端云联合在线预测，带宽成本-3%以上；二是可信播控，按观播时长调整目标缓存水位，短视频下压省成本、长视频上调减卡顿；三是按秒预加载，基于 MP4 封装特点将按时长决策预加载大小与按Size混合，提升中长视频起播速度。全链路缓存（2023）改进进一步用条件期望 替代固定配置值。 针对全局曲线无法区分用户差异的问题，按画质敏感用户、画质敏感视频等群体标签对曲线参数做差异化调整，端上超分的考量也在此阶段加入，按设备 CPU/GPU/ 内存能力圈选适用范围并结合实时负载设置运行条件，证明了个性化的必要性——同样档位对不同用户和设备的收益成本比不同。分群后的映射为： Vision（2025） 将选档、超分、锐化和解码降级纳入同一决策体系，通过明确接口实现联合优化而非用模型替代，超分决策模块判断各档位是否适合超分及方式并将增强后画质反馈给选档，播放性能预估模块将候选档位的画质、卡顿与设备负载映射为统一性能价值，选档模块比较「档位 × 增强动作」的综合影响，单步目标函数为： （往左滑动查看完整公式） 使用 MPC 在播放列表时域上滚动求解未来动作序列： Vision 还引入了用户维度的个性化，基于历史卡顿事件构建了用户卡顿退出率画像，对退出率高的用户提高流畅性权重，对耐受度高的用户保留更多画质空间。实验显示卡顿退出率 -2% 以上，起播稳定性和播放流畅度显著优化，在播放时长增长的同时，码率降低还带来了较大幅度成本收益。 图5：Vision 的综合信号层与动作决策层架构，含信号接入、决策信号加工、动作决策与反馈闭环 3.3 客户端选路：ParaFlow与PRIME ParaFlow 与 PRIME 回答的问题主要是「数据走哪条路径、用哪个网络资源」，移动设备常在 Wi-Fi 与蜂窝多路径间切换，路径质量时刻波动，客户端选路需要在多路径、多资源间做实时择优，其中 ParaFlow 是多路径选路的框架名，下文的 CROSS 与 Amphi 分别是它的两代实现，PRIME 则把决策对象从路径指向网络资源。 多路选择在业内不算很新的概念，但其他公司、团队或者上线者寥寥，或者并未达到足以令人满意的效果，学术界或者其他公司在此的尝试，弊病有时在于对于算法化「不够相信」或者「理解不深」，有时在于缺乏对基建的充分理解，假设失配或者先验误设。 可以例证的是，在形如 PRIME 的工作中，通过将优化目标直接与业务收益（包括用户指标、营收指标和成本）挂钩，就带来了巨大的价值，过程中较难的部分并非算法设计或者调参，而是在于长周期内，对底层工程链路的拆解重写，令其对齐建模时的相关基础假设。 CROSS 同时优化的是数据路径与 ACK 路径，数据侧发起两个并行下载任务，每次下载绑定一条路径，从源头减少跨路径乱序，buffer 告急时动态回退 minRTT 调度补带宽，ACK 侧对带宽、单向时延、丢包率归一化后加权打分，并针对 LTE 的上行瓶颈与 Wi-Fi 双向竞争做了差异化修正，按综合得分择优： （往左滑动查看完整公式） 该版本基于XQUIC，吞吐+25%~38%，卡顿最高-52%，论文参考： CROSS: A Dual-Sided Scheduling Framework for Efficient Multipath Video Streaming (http://iir.ruc.edu.cn/~litong/papers/Cross-A%20Dual-Sided%20Scheduling%20Framework%20for%20Efficient%20Multipath%20Video%20Streaming.pdf) Amphi 针对「用户随时滑走」与「移动网络波动」并存的短视频场景做跨层协同，应用层的多流调度器同时为多个候选视频分配带宽，减少卡顿与无效下载，传输层的多路径调度器将每路流分发至多条网络路径，增强对 Wi-Fi/ 蜂窝波动的鲁棒性，两层之间通过 ACK 反馈联动，这样多流 × 多路径的联合带宽分配可形式化为： （往左滑动查看完整公式） 其中为流𝒮在路径𝒫上分配的速率，Cₚ为由ACK反馈实时估计的路径容量，Uₛ(·)为流𝒮的边际效用函数，应用层多流调度与传输层多路径调度共享同一分配结果，并随 ACK 反馈滚动更新。该版本 QoE+18.6%~75.2%，带宽浪费 -6.3%~13.4%。 图6：Amphi 的应用层多流调度器与传输层多路径调度器通过 ACK 反馈联动 PRIME（2026） 的思路是，把决策对象从「路径」指向「网络资源」，综合各资源的实时性能、带宽单价、用户播放状态与个性化观播时长估计体验收益，在候选资源集合中做「体验收益-带宽成本」的统一权衡并灵活切换，在抖音上线过程中已累计取得约 -8.5% 的带宽收益，其决策可写为： 论文参考：PIRA: Pan-CDN Intra-video Resource Adaptation for Short Video Streaming(https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.18606) 3.4 网络测速：单队列 vs SHEF 网络测速 面向的是这样一个问题：「当前有多少网络资源可用」，它本身不做播放决策，但会作为 Demand、Vision 和其他算法策略的共同输入，测速偏低会直接压低码率，因此它的鲁棒性还决定了其他下载策略能否顺利上线。 网络测速算法的输出是客户端音视频算法的基础输入，本身存在多年，原始版本行业通用，十分简单有效，并且经过了多种对比评估，证明其他许多精巧的设计并不能带来增益；但另一方面，抖音在经过仔细观察，仍然可以做出形如SHEF的改进并带来直接效果，这个事实再次、明确地提醒我们：一切价值均可结合环境重估，基础环节仍可改进。 单队列测速（2019） 即常见的被动式单队列架构，播放下载组件的 Range 下载完成回调产生一个采样点，送入定长 FIFO 队列统一给出估计，默认算法为加权中位数，以每次下载的数据量Sᵢ为权重，取累计权重首次过半的采样点，避免异常采样拉偏结果： 算法本身较为简单基础，同期也试过 MLP、GBR 回归预测网速等各种策略，但队列长度超过 15 后改善很小，认知为移动网络波动大导致时序预测空间有限，因此很长时间内仍以加权中位数为主要默认算法。 鲁棒性修正（2023） 不是针对算法精度修改，主因是观测被其他策略污染，Range 的缩小抬高了建联开销占比、缓存控制又减少了高网速时段采样、多样化 CDN 资源与分片并行下载等都会改变观测值，结果是码率沦为其他策略调整的副产品，所以在不改主框架的情况下，可以叠加几项修正，其中建联开销修正由 反解得到： 为窗口内平均任务大小，为建联开销粗估值，静态基准用于把该开销的影响固定，迭代方向是引入更多 RTT 特征、改为预估指定分片的下载耗时，并按 CDN 类型分别估计等。 SHEF（Stratified Heterogeneous Estimation Fusion，2026） 的目的是更彻底地解决单队列的结构性局限，由于采样只在下载完成时产生，更新频率受下载节奏支配，稳态播放下采样间隔可达数秒，网络劣化时只能沿用很旧的估计。SHEF 相当于把「窗口取长还是取短」的 trade-off 从窗口移到加权的维度，即将下载完成、过程、超时等不同类别事件分入不同队列，再按网络状态加权融合： （往左滑动查看完整公式） 不同采样共享同一数据结构，仅以事件类型区分语义，让测速值在连续下载中持续变化，配合突变弱网检测影响下载决策，替换后带来 LT 上升、画质提升、卡顿率下降、成本下降等收益。 04 | 小结 在团队过往的总结中，曾经定义了 L1-L5 级别的个性化能力标准，虽然当前抖音仍在 L4 的层次上前行—— 对齐最先进的个性化技术 建立千级别的干预点 支持半自动化挖掘新干预点和自动化评估 支持高阶信号如长序列、多模态等 支持业务影响视角进行特征构建，支持通过数据挖掘驱动特征构建 视频和用户全类型覆盖 达到十万分之一的业务优化精度 ...... 但随着 AI 浪潮近几年的推动，L5 等级所描述的全系统、全链路精准感知与计算，自动化拓展状态空间，策略统筹、模型精度方面达成理论最优等目标，也并非天方夜谭、遥不可及，期待后续抖音可以将技术理想实践落地，为用户带来极限的音视频体验。 阅读原文 跳转微信打开

items.title: 沙龙回顾｜快手披露万人组织的企业AI生产力实践路径
items.summary: 快手技术 2026-11-02 20:25 北京 文末领取讲师PPT! 10月31日，快手技术沙龙第六期在北京举办。本期沙龙以“从研发效能走向企业AI生产力”为主题，来自快手、OPPO及软件工程领域的多位技术专家，共同探讨AI如何从个人提效工具走向企业级生产力，并分享组织建设、智能体工程化、业务规模化提效与智能评测等一线实践。 沙龙现场，快手企业AI生产力副总裁王诩在致辞中表示，AI在带来研发生产力变革的同时，也面临Token费用持续上升、重复建设与安全风险等现实问题。大模型存在不确定性，需要通过工程手段保证安全、稳定与效果；企业AI生产力同样需要通过工程、组织与管理手段，让AI走进研发、业务场景乃至HR、财务等工作领域。他将快手AI在企业中的发展总结为实践、产品与工具推广、岗位职责调整、自上而下组织变革四个阶段，今年9月成立的企业AI生产力（iWork）组织，正是组织变革这一步的落地。 快手企业AI生产力副总裁 王诩 从工程师到全员、从团队到组织，快手iWork演进路径 快手企业智能体建设负责人、企业AI生产力专家沈浪介绍，快手的企业AI生产力实践最初是从工程师提效切入的。2025年起，快手围绕本地AI Coding工具CodeFlicker和云端研发平台KATE，逐步把需求分析、代码评审、测试用例和线上监控等能力Agent化，并将研发范式分为由人主导AI辅助的L1，强调人机协同完成需求交付的L2，以及由AI承担更多自主开发、人负责审核的L3。沈浪透露，该阶段目标是在2026年底把快手所有线上交付需求的80%提升到L2水平，当前已超过70%。 沙龙活动现场 转折发生在2026年Q2，AI开始从服务工程师走向服务更多员工。大量非技术用户开始借助CodeFlicker做演示文稿、调研和数据分析，快手由此将编程助手与Work形态产品整合为通用Agent MyFlicker，面向全员开放，截至2026年7月，MyFlicker周活跃用户数较2025年末增加约2.5倍。 随着使用范围扩大，Token成本也成为企业规模化应用AI需要关注的问题。快手通过推行“Token积分制”，将预算折算成积分下发至员工，让员工自主选择如何使用；并通过“AI蹭饭研判官”“AI贪吃蛇大赛”“PDE集结令”等“全民AI”活动降低使用门槛，PDE集结令最终收到4000余个作品，验证了非技术人群构建工具的可能性。 年中复盘时，沈浪发现个体提效不等于组织提效，有两大问题制约组织效率，一是“孤岛区”，强AI能力员工的方法未沉淀，无法辐射团队；二是“空转区”，团队引入大量数字员工却因协作链路上下文不完整导致效率平平。 此后，快手将探索重点从个体推进到团队。沈浪将其核心规律概括为“先蒸馏，再折叠”，先把团队经验沉淀为AI可消费的知识、Skill和工作流，让AI进入真实工作，再招募数字员工在团队中独立完成重复性、确定性工作，最后再基于新的工作方式调整人与人之间的分工，让更多人聚焦到更多创造类、高价值工作上。基于这些实践，把MyFlicker升级到了2.0，可以为每个团队建设团队Agent。目前，团队AI已在快手内部规模化推广，约有500多个团队Agent、1000多个数字员工独立工作，几乎覆盖技术、销售、设计等所有团队。 到2026年Q4，快手的探索开始从团队走向组织。面对数百人规模的组织，单纯复制团队Agent无法解决复杂工作流与多系统协同问题。快手由此成立iWork，并探索MyFlicker 3.0，通过增加“AI工作台”，将原本分散的系统、流程和企业上下文转化为AI可调用的能力，建立企业级AI基座，推进全组织AI化。 从Demo走向生产，工程体系成为关键 沈浪用快手的实践印证了 "个体提效不等于组织提效"，《软件工程3.0》作者、同济大学特聘教授朱少民则从第一性原理出发，回答了“AI落地为什么需要工程体系”。他指出，企业AI落地需要警惕三个假象：生成不等于完成，个人效率不等于组织吞吐，Demo成功也不等于生产可靠。在此基础上，他提出一个生产力公式：企业生产力＝可交付客户价值÷总投入。如果效率提升伴随着质量、可交付率和可治理性下降，企业生产力未必真正提高。 《软件工程3.0》作者、同济大学特聘教授 朱少民 “大模型决定了智能研发的天花板，而工程体系决定了我们能摸到多高。”朱少民认为，未来企业智能研发的竞争焦点将不再只是模型能力，也包括工程体系是否完善。为此，企业需要建立“规约工程、驾驭工程、质量门禁”三位一体的工程体系：用可验证的方式明确目标、上下文、禁止事项和验收标准；利用记忆、工具权限和Agent框架约束执行；在代码、测试、交付和运行阶段建立失败升级与回滚机制。 对于具体演进路径，朱少民提出可以分三步推进：首先进行架构清理和知识沉淀，为Agent参与研发打好基础；其次搭建Harness框架，为Agent自主执行任务提供工程环境；最后构建质量门禁和反馈闭环，让Agent在可验证、可治理的前提下逐步提高自主执行能力。 随着Agent承担更多生成和执行任务，研发团队的能力结构也将发生变化。在朱少民看来，业务需求、系统架构和质量判断等能力将更加重要，产品经理、架构师与质量专家的价值也会进一步凸显。 从“超级个体”到“臭鼬工厂”，快手探索组织变革新模式 个人能力和平台能力具备之后，如何让AI真正改善端到端交付，成为下一道难题。快手磁力引擎风控技术负责人王东旭分享了所在团队从“OPC超级个体”走向“液态组织”，再到“臭鼬工厂”的探索过程。 快手磁力引擎风控技术负责人 王东旭 王东旭所在团队规模超百人，覆盖产品、运营、研发、算法和测试等职能，团队最初选择少数成员在真实业务中验证AI能否帮助个人跨越原有专业边界。例如，一名应用算法工程师独立完成AI深伪检测平台，另一名成员在25天内全栈交付反作弊洞察平台。 但超级个体的出现并没有自动解决排期等待和跨角色协作问题。团队随后推进算法与工程边界融合、技术让渡和前后端全栈转型，将部分Prompt配置与交互式运营能力交给更接近业务的运营人员，算法与工程人员则转向更复杂的算法和系统架构工作。 “全栈不是多做一份工，而是少等一个人。”王东旭表示。即使编码效率大幅提升，只要需求分析、协作、测试和发布等环节仍存在等待，局部提速就很难变成端到端收益。他借助阿姆达尔定律解释，如果编码环节只占端到端耗时的20%，即使将其压缩至接近零，整体交付速度增幅也只有约25%。“技术的天花板是数学题，组织的天花板是决策题。” 为进一步减少协调成本，团队借鉴洛克希德·马丁“臭鼬工厂”的组织思路，通过“绑目标、缩节点、搬工位”三类动作，让产品、运营、研发、算法和测试围绕同一目标集中协作，并将需求流转节点从12个缩减至6个，减少纯协调环节。在一项局部试点中，29名成员覆盖3个业务方向，需求吞吐率由36%升至84%，需求交付周期压缩至原来的五分之一，全栈交付需求数增至此前的9倍，并完成19个PDE需求。 王东旭同时强调，“臭鼬工厂”并非适用于所有场景。复杂存量核心系统、强跨团队依赖，以及无法保证人员集中投入或缺少合适负责人的场景，现阶段并不适合采用这一模式。在他看来，“一个臭鼬工厂是特例，一群臭鼬工厂才是能力”。 构建需求测试分级体系，让AI更好地测试AI 当研发速度被AI大幅拉快，质量如何守住？快手磁力引擎风控质量负责人吕冬冬给出了“需求测试分级、风险挖掘与Agentic AI Testing”的实践框架。 快手磁力引擎风控质量负责人 吕冬冬 吕冬冬指出，传统质量体系面临全量验证难以持续、人力无法线性扩张、过程指标难以代表真实质量等问题。快手相关大部门据此构建了基于“云帆”平台的智能分级体系，把是否涉及资金、主链路、历史故障和安全等判断注入Agent，形成高中低三类策略：高风险需求由人工主导、AI辅助；中风险需求采用人机协同；在其所在风控业务中，部分低风险需求由AI承担更多验证，人工负责抽检与异常升级。 更关键的是“AI测AI”的同源闭环问题：如果写代码、写用例和判质量均由Agent完成，测试通过可能只说明系统内部自洽，并不必然意味着结果正确。吕冬冬介绍，相关实践正在通过异源模型分工、固定评测集与黄金真值、差分及变异测试和人工校准等方式降低同源偏差，并坚持“依据证据而非结论”的门禁原则。他强调，未来质量团队的角色将从执行者转向质量规则制定者，在策略定义与最终准出上保留人的责任。 随着AI能力演进，吕冬冬指出，质量责任正在沿交付链路前移，从人工测试和工程自动化进一步走向AI与PDE协同。测试工程师的价值正从“做得快”转向“判断得准”，从执行者转变为规则制定者。 OPPO互联网的AI Native落地实践 OPPO产研提效产品负责人郝刚则分享了OPPO互联网业务在AI Native组织演进中的探索：从工具普及、个人提效，到组织提效，再进一步探索AI Native组织。 OPPO产研提效产品负责人 郝刚 在工具普及阶段，OPPO互联网业务将AI引入编程、测试、运营、审核、游戏和设计等日常工作，并通过AI README让项目代码和规范更容易被AI理解，同时逐步搭建研发数字人、模型广场、知识库，以及Skill和MCP中心等平台能力。 随着AI工具逐渐普及，OPPO也发现，个人效率提升并不意味着团队交付效率同步提高。为此，OPPO开始提高研发流程中AI能够参与和掌控的环节占比，并重点推进两件事：建设高质量知识库，以及打造能够持续演进的AI交付工作流，以扩大AI协同交付的覆盖范围，减少重复交接和等待。 在组织层面，OPPO先选择部分人员开展AI转型试验，再逐步推进业务流程重构、专业能力沉淀和平台底座建设。其CoMind智能体协同交付平台尝试组织需求、方案、研发与验证等环节的Agent协同，并在部分B端场景继续向发布链路延伸。郝刚同时指出，复杂C端及多端发布仍有较多人工参与，AI Native改造尚未完成。 对于如何走向AI Native，郝刚认为，需要自上而下与自下而上两条路径共同推进：管理者既要亲自上手，也要判断转型方向；员工则需要从超级个体走向协同的“蜂群”，让判断、执行和经验彼此连接，形成团队复利。 从研发提效到组织跃迁，从超级个体到臭鼬工厂，从人工验证到智能评测，本场沙龙五位嘉宾的分享指向同一判断：AI的价值不只取决于单点工具的提效幅度，更取决于组织能否把分散在个体身上的经验沉淀为可复用的团队资产，并进一步升级为面向组织的生产力基础设施。当模型能力逐渐成为通用基础能力，谁能率先完成知识、流程与协作方式的系统性重构，谁才更有可能把AI的技术红利转化为可持续的组织生产力。 左右滑动查看更多 items.title: 美团正式发布 LongCat-2.5：面向智能体任务的原生多模态模型
items.summary: 美团正式发布 LongCat-2.5，这是一个面向长程智能体任务的原生多模态模型。模型总参数量为 1.6 万亿，每个 token 激活约 480 亿参数，在 LongCat-2.0 的基础上进一步强化了原生视觉理解与智能体编程能力。 新模型在长程智能体任务中有明显效果提升，这源于我们在长序列训练中加入了更多长程轨迹数据，并通过大规模长程强化学习，提升模型在复杂代码库开发、完整项目构建等任务中的端到端工程能力。围绕数据合成、环境构建与跨 Harness 混合训练，我们持续扩展这条训练链路。此外，我们也将真实 Agent 的失败轨迹转化为可复现、可验证的训练任务，针对模型能力短板持续补充训练数据。 与此同时，LongCat-2.5 具备原生视觉理解能力，可将视觉信号表示为多层级离散 token，使主干模型以统一的 token 形式处理视觉与文本输入，在 Visual Coding 上表现出色，并支持创意设计和 3D 等任务。 这些升级背后，是持续演进的基础设施：我们优化了国产算力上的长上下文训练与 W4A4 推理，并通过训推数值一致性和长上下文 rollout 优化，支撑大规模长程 RL 的高效运行。 指标看板 为直观呈现 LongCat-2.5 当前的能力水平，我们在下图中选取 GPT-5.5、GPT-5.6-Sol、Claude-Opus-4.8 和 Claude-Opus-5 进行对比。涵盖更多模型的详细评测结果见后文表格。 01 视觉表征建模 LongCat-2.5 将视觉信号表示为多层级离散 token，使主干模型以统一的 token 形式处理视觉与文本输入。这一设计融合了原生分辨率视觉离散化、离线视觉预处理，以及与主干模型联合学习的视觉 embedding，既能支持原生多模态融合，也简化了训练中的视觉计算与负载管理。 离散原生分辨率视觉 Transformer：为使视觉基元建模具备与语言建模类似的 token 级抽象，我们将视觉信号表示为多层级词表 token。沿用 LongCat-Next[1]的方法，对语义对齐编码器（Semantic-and-Aligned Encoder，SAE）产生的原生分辨率特征应用残差向量量化（Residual Vector Quantization，RVQ），解决视觉离散化的信息瓶颈。 图 1：原生分辨率视觉离散化——将不同分辨率的图像编码为离散 token 序列，并通过视觉解码器重建图像 离线视觉 token 预处理：为减少在线视觉计算和工作负载异构性，固定的 tokenizer 允许我们离线预计算并缓存视觉 token ID。主干模型因此直接处理预先分词的序列，简化长序列打包与切分，并改善分布式训练的负载均衡。 原生视觉表示：视觉码本 embedding 与主干模型联合学习。在平均激活参数约为 3B 的较小规模 MoE 模型上，初步验证显示，视觉与文本 embedding 在 t-SNE 可视化中呈交织分布，表明两者在共享语义空间中的融合。 图 2：视觉与文本 embedding 的 t-SNE 对比。右图为平均激活参数约 3B 的 MoE 模型上的验证结果 02 大规模智能体强化学习 RL scaling 是提升模型智能的关键步骤。我们为 LongCat-2.5 搭建了全面的 Agentic RL 训练链路，从数据、环境、算法和 Harness 等方面对长程任务进行大规模扩展。 图 3：面向长程任务的 agentic RL 训练链路，涵盖数据与环境、异步训练、奖励设计和混合训练 大规模数据合成与环境构建：我们构建可扩展的数据合成流水线，自动化生成训练任务、可交互环境和可验证的测试用例，数据来源涵盖 GitHub 公开仓库和内部真实场景的代码任务。对于筛选后的 PR 和关联 issue，利用 Agent 自动打标、合成环境，并进行 fail-to-pass（F2P）和 pass-to-pass（P2P）测试校验。在 RL 训练中，实时 rollout 的轨迹和通过率辅助我们进行二次数据打标和筛选，并基于假阴、假阳分析持续修正和扩充 F2P 测试用例，提高对任务功能描述的覆盖率，和验证信号的准确性。 异步强化学习与稳定性优化：我们采用 partial rollout 异步训练策略缓解长尾效率问题：每个 RL step 保持一定过采样率，凑齐批次后中断、保存未完成轨迹，并在下一采样阶段恢复。过采样率基于任务通过率调整，并过滤全对或全错的零梯度样本组，以保证有效梯度。Partial rollout 中，同一轨迹的 token 可能来自不同历史 checkpoint，带来样本陈旧性。为保证训练稳定性，我们裁剪采样时与当前训练时 logprob 的差异，并基于历史累计差异调整每个 token 的梯度贡献，限制陈旧性带来的梯度偏置；此外，从 infra 视角提供了训推一致性的优化方案。 Reward hacking 与输出行为优化：我们通过在任务环境中断网、清除 git 历史和文件缓存，并引入 LLM judge 监督轨迹，以限制模型的投机行为。在输出行为优化上，我们对重复思考和重复工具调用施加额外惩罚；对过度思考和长度增长过快的问题，则通过重新分配正样本中的 Reward 加以抑制。 混合训练与泛化：模型在 RL 中可自主学习和适配近似任务和 Harness。前置冷启阶段仅需覆盖少量适配 scaffold 用例，在 RL 阶段，通过跨多任务和跨 scaffold 的混合训练可显著提高模型泛化能力，并促进不同任务上的性能提升。 03 多专家在线教学 为将各领域能力融入主线模型，我们沿用 LongCat-2.0 的专家组机制，分别优化 Agent 能力、推理能力和交互体验，涵盖多轮任务执行、单轮推理、细粒度指令遵循，以及不牺牲有用性的安全防御。在 MOPD 中，学生模型在各领域任务中在线采样，领域专家通过采样结果上的全词表 KL 散度[2]训练学生。 样本既要反映学生的实际任务行为，也要让教师给出可信的学习信号。为限制分布偏移，先前工作将教师在 SFT 或 RL 阶段见过的轨迹拆为 per-turn prefix，作为学生采样的上下文。我们进一步将每轮教师回复按固定长度拆为 per-cut prefix，并将学生自采样的最大长度限制为该值，以处理单轮长回复中的分布偏移。 图 4：用于学生在线采样的 per-cut prefix 为控制计算与存储成本，同一教师轨迹的 prefix 被分为一组，送至同一推理引擎，共享 prefill 计算与 KV cache。训练时，以教师轨迹为树干、学生采样为分支构建树，结合 Tree Attention[3]，通过单次前传与反传完成同组所有样本的 OPD 训练，避免教师轨迹上的冗余计算与存储。 04 国产算力上的长上下文训练 LongCat-2.5 在中训练和监督微调阶段均采用长序列训练。针对国产算力单卡显存不足 80 GB 的限制，训练系统重点优化显存开销，并围绕超节点架构设计并行策略。 4.1 面向超节点的并行策略 LongCat-2.5 根据超节点拓扑配置并行组，FSDP 和 EP 并行度均与单个超节点的卡数一致，CP 并行度不超过该卡数，使参数 AllGather、专家 token AllToAll 和 KV AllGather 均在超节点内的高带宽互联域中完成。 混合词表并行在 DP 和 CP 联合并行域内对基础词嵌入层、LM head 和 N-gram 嵌入层进行分片，进一步降低显存占用。 针对大规模专家并行中的负载不均衡问题，LongCat-2.5 基于 MoonEP 引入阈值触发的动态专家复制机制。仅当 EP 负载不均衡程度达到预设阈值时才启用复制，以避免额外通信开销超过负载均衡收益，并防止路由 token 引发接收端显存溢出、通信操作引发发送端显存溢出。 提前图像 token 生成使训练计算图不再包含视觉编码器，简化了并行实现。利用已知的图像 token 数量，系统可以在数据打包和打散时预估各模态的负载比例，使各数据并行 rank 上的模态占比接近。 4.2 FSDP 与系统优化 LongCat-2.5 引入双重分片 FSDP，模型参数在超节点内的 FSDP 域中分片，FP32 主权重和优化器状态则通过 HSDP 副本进一步跨 FSDP 域分片，在保持参数通信效率的同时，降低常驻显存。 参数、梯度和优化器状态统一组织为连续的扁平化缓冲区，支持非均匀分片和 Muon 优化器分片。同时，通过直接写入权重梯度、复用临时缓冲区，减少中间拷贝，降低峰值显存占用。 系统采用零拷贝 AllGather/ReduceScatter，消除默认通信算法引入的中间拷贝。EP 将 token 与路由概率打包传输，并采用基于 AIV 的通信实现，缓解 AICPU 任务展开瓶颈。参数预取使 AllGather 与计算重叠执行，同时控制与 CP 的资源竞争；ScMoE 则使 EP 通信与稠密分支计算重叠执行。 系统通过批量执行梯度操作、合并指标归约、CPU 绑核和 NUMA 感知调度，降低主机侧开销。 综合上述优化，该 FSDP 配置在长序列 SFT 任务中的单卡吞吐量较 DDP 基线提升 86%。 图 5：国产 AI 加速器上的长上下文训练 05 智能体强化学习基础设施 5.1 训推精度一致性 基于 IsoExec[4]、GLM-5[5] 和 XoRL[6]的工作，我们构建了生产级训推一致性方案，使训练、Prefill 和 Decode 可独立选择并行配置，在性能接近无损的同时，保持逐 token logprob 的 bitwise 一致。训推两端统一采用高效的 batch-invariant 算子并对齐框架计算逻辑，补齐 backward 支持。该方案已在实验和生产任务中默认启用，为算子与框架迭代提供统一的数值回归基准。针对因为不同并行方式导致的训推无法对齐的问题，我们在社区的方案上进一步扩展 TP 和 DCP 的训推一致性支持。 TP：以完整 K 维计算替代分段求和，性能接近无损。训练侧保留权重分片，通过权重 All-Gather 和输入 AlltoAll，独立完成完整 K 维 GEMM，无需对局部结果进行 Reduce-Scatter 求和。Prefill 沿用该方案；Decode 则将 o_proj/fc2 改为 column-parallel，通过输入 All-Gather、完整 K 维 GEMM 和输出 AlltoAll 完成计算，既避免每步聚合完整权重，也避免跨卡数值求和。 DCP：在训练与 Prefill 中复现 Decode 的累加路径。我们在训练 forward 和推理 Prefill 中接入配套的 sparse attention 算子，复现指定 DCP 配置下 Decode 的 KV 分块与归约顺序，对齐了三者的计算精度。 5.2 长上下文 rollout 优化 针对负载可控的长上下文多轮 rollout，我们采用 PD 分离，为 Prefill 和 Decode 分别选择合适的并行策略，并从缓存存储、跨层卸载和请求调度三个方面协同优化： 扩大有效缓存容量：Prefill 采用 QCP 按 token 分配计算、KVP 按页分散存储，避免 MLA 下 TP 切分带来的 KV 冗余。HiCache 在 KV 回迁显存后，释放无其他读取引用的主存副本，减少两级缓存重复占用；同时基于 Mooncake 重构权重管理与 Actor offload 方案，为 HiCache 释放更多内存。 通过跨层预取隐藏搬运开销：利用 LSA[7] 奇数层复用前一偶数层 top-k 索引的特点，将奇数层完整 KV 卸载至主存，显存仅保留小容量工作缓存。偶数层产生索引后，提前加载下一奇数层所需 KV，并与当前层后续计算重叠，在 TPOT 无损的情况下使 Decode KV 缓存容量接近翻倍。 通过容量感知调度避免重算雪崩：Router 根据 L1+L2 缓存容量和请求 token 总量控制请求放行，并优先推进完成度较高的 Group，尽早凑齐训练批次、释放缓存，避免多条长轨迹交替推进时反复淘汰彼此前缀，引发大规模重算。 图 6：所测长上下文负载的 Prefill/Decode 配置；在该场景下，P/D 实例配比 3:2 性能最优 06 W4A4 高效推理 针对 1.6T 级 MoE 模型，我们结合模型结构与国产 AI 加速器的硬件特性，围绕量化精度、底层算子与推理流水开展协同优化，构建 W4A4 高效推理方案。 该方案将专家权重与激活同时量化至 4 bit，并通过原生 INT4 矩阵乘法单元执行相应的矩阵计算。 在精度方面，以 FlatQuant 的可学习等价变换为基础，进一步优化 MoE 模型的量化精度，在已评测的各项下游任务上保持与量化前模型相当的表现。 在算子与数据路径方面，通过专家共享的输入变换，在 token 复制与分发前完成量化，使同一份 INT4 表示贯穿专家通信与计算。将变换、尺度计算、量化和打包融合到专用算子，并结合权重布局与转置访问优化，减少数据搬运和转换开销。 在系统层面，针对 prefill 与 decode 的执行特点，依据模型的数据依赖和硬件资源约束，优化计算与通信的流水重叠。 在线上压测中，相对 W8A8 INT8 基线，prefill 和 decode 吞吐分别提升 43.3% 和 42.77%，TTFT 和 TPOT 分别降低 15.91% 和 19.72%。在算子层面，GMM 相对 W8A8 实现平均 1.73× 加速。 07 能力演示 能力演示 08 评测说明 详情参见官网技术博客：https://longcat.ai/blog/longcat-2.5。 引用 [1] LongCat-Next 方法：https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27538 [2] 全词表 KL 散度：https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/main/DeepSeek_V41_Tech_Report.pdf [3] Tree Attention：https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.07606 [4] IsoExec：https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-08-21-isoexec [5] GLM-5：https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/2262 [6] XoRL：https://kiddyboots216.github.io/mismatch/ [7] LSA：https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01662 体验入口 注册认证即赠千万 token，老用户加赠五百万 token，新模型限时福利已上线！ items.title: 让 AI 看得见、判得准、改得对—— D2C 从设计稿到三端真机达标的自动化实践
items.summary: 原创 用户&内容技术 2026-11-02 11:47 浙江 给 AI 装上眼睛，让设计稿自动变真机代码。 本文介绍了 D2C（设计稿到代码）在移动端自动化落地的实践方案。针对 AI 生码后无法感知真机渲染效果、难以自我验收的痛点，团队构建了一套端上 UI Harness 体系，通过 Loop Engineering 让 AI 实现“生码-编译-三端真机验证-自动修复”的全流程闭环。核心思路是重新划分程序与 AI 的边界：将确定性流程下沉至 CLI 骨架执行，AI 仅保留少量推理决策点；同时结合像素 diff、DOM 树对比等多层信号融合技术为 AI 装上“眼睛”，并辅以交叉验证与独立门禁防止假交付。该方案已打通 DX、Weex、Muise 三条链路，用户只需提交设计稿即可全自动完成达标交付，并沉淀了五条可迁移的 Agent 工程化方法论。 开场 · 一个现实的问题 先抛一个问题: AI 已经能一句话生一张UI卡片代码，但你敢直接把 AI 生出来的代码提测上线吗？ 大概率不敢，因为你大概率经历过这样的场景：AI 信心满满地报告"卡片已完成"，你推到真机一看——布局错位了、badge 圆角被截了、价格符号 ¥ 和数字没对齐、 一端上正常但另一端上文字截断了。 AI 不知道自己写错了。它没有眼睛，看不到真机上渲染出来到底是什么样。 背景 · AI 生码之后,谁来验收? AI 会写代码,这在 2026 年已经不是新闻。真正的问题是:AI 写完之后,谁来验收? 行业正在形成一个共识:Agent = Harness + LLM —— 光有模型能力远远不够,Agent 能不能可靠工作,取决于外面套的那层工程脚手架(Harness)。而这层脚手架的质量,可以拆成三件事: 质量 = 输入约束 × 生成约束 × 验证闭环 输入约束:给 AI 看什么上下文(读懂项目代码、拿到设计稿数据、了解业务规则) 生成约束:让 AI 按什么规范写(编码规范、组件复用、目录约定) 验证闭环:AI 写完之后,自己知道对不对、能自己迭代修复 前两项,业界已经有相对成熟的方案。但第三项 —— 验证闭环 —— 在移动端是断的。 Web 端早就闭合了这个环:Playwright 跑截图、Chrome DevTools 拿日志、Headless Browser 做回归 —— AI 生完码,自己跑一遍就知道对不对。但移动端呢? AI 写完一个 DX 卡片或 Weex 组件,它看不到真机上渲染成什么样、判不了对和错、更不会自己迭代优化。 具体到 D2C(Design to Code)场景,断裂带体现为三个具体问题: 问题一 · AI 生完码就"闭眼交卷" 拿不到真机截图、判不了视觉还原度、不会自己迭代修复。常常"看起来 OK"就交付 —— 结果 badge 圆角被截了、暗黑模式颜色错了、鸿蒙上文字截断了。AI 自己完全不知道。 问题二 · 三端渲染差异靠人肉 iOS、Android、鸿蒙 的字体栅格化、单位换算(px / dp)、暗黑模式行为各不相同 —— 同一份代码在三端上渲染出来是三个样子,上线前必须人工三端都验一遍，AI一个验证不了。 问题三 · 端上 UI 技术栈碎片化 团队业务同时跑着 多套渲染框架,每接一条链路,都要从零造一遍验证工具 —— 工作量比较大。 这些都不是模型能力问题,是 Harness 工程问题 —— 验证闭环这一环,在移动端比较缺失。 所以我们决定做一件事:建一个 D2C Harness 打通三端真机验证闭环 —— 让 AI 自己看到真机、自己判断对不对、自己改到达标。把移动端的验证断裂带,像 Web 端一样闭合起来。 AI 生码不难,难的是让 AI 自己知道自己写对了 —— 这就是验证闭环。 结果 过去一段时间，我们做了一件事：把 D2C 从"设计稿生完码就结束"，升级到"从设计稿出发，AI 一路自己走完生码、编译、三端真机验证，直到视觉还原达标"。 用户使用方式:内部研发平台创建Issue ，贴设计稿链接 和代码仓库，剩下的 AI 自动完成 —— 生码、编译、三端真机截图、diff 对比、迭代修复、代码提交 —— 全程不需要人。 ▐ 3.1 真机交互体验 ▐3.2 UI优化页面 设计思考 · 不只是生码工具， 而是一套端上 UI 的 Harness 体系 如果 D2C 只是一个生码工具，那 AI 生完码就结束了，剩下的编译、预览、验证、修复全靠人——断裂带还是断的。 我们要做的不是"更好的生码工具"，而是一套面向端上 UI 的 Harness 体系——把 AI 生码之后的所有环节都工程化地闭合起来： 环节 AI 自由发挥能做到吗 Harness 做什么 编译 能写代码，但编译报错了不一定能自己修 编译门禁 + 自动重试 + 结构化错误反馈 真机预览 看不到真机 三端云真机自动推送 + 组件级截图 视觉验证 说不清"像不像" 像素级 diff + 热力图 + 90 分硬门槛 修复迭代 不知道哪里错、改完不知道有没有改好 AI 看 diff → 改码 → 再验 → 回退保护 交付 可能提前宣称"完成了" 门禁校验 + 自动 CR + 交付报告 ▐4.1 传统 D2C vs 我们的 D2C 维度 过去的做法 我们的做法 输入要求 切好的设计稿 · 图层命名规范 给人看的 PRD + 设计稿链接 验证方式 H5 模拟预览 三端真机截图 + 像素级 diff 还原度判断 人肉看"差不多就行" 硬门槛 · 不达标自动迭代 修复方式 人工修改 → 重新生成 AI 看 diff 热力图 → 改码 → 重新验证 交付物 一份代码 代码 + 三端截图 + diff 报告 + CR 运行方式 人坐在 IDE 前操作 Issue 驱动 · 全自动 Agent ▐4.2 让 AI 少做事 · 结果反而更可靠 我们踩过一个坑：一开始，我们把所有步骤写进一份近千行的 SKILL 说明书，让 AI 照着一步步执行。逻辑很自然——步骤写得越细，AI 应该做得越好，对吧？ 结果恰恰相反： 漏步骤率 ~30%：明确写了"按 1→2→3→…→9 执行"，AI 实际跑的是 1→2→4→7→9 幻觉式完成：AI 自信地输出"步骤 3 已完成"，但实际从未调用对应工具 2 小时白干：其中 40 分钟卡在"等截图超时"——这种事根本不需要 AI 判断，一个 if file.exists() 就够了 根因只有一句话：把确定性流程塞进了概率性 prompt。 我们回头分析那份 SKILL，发现 大部分的内容是流程编排——分支切换、编译重试、URL 管理、截图轮询——这些操作的容都是可以固化为程序代码的。但我们把它们交给了一个本质上是"大概率会照做"的概率系统。 CLI化改造 改造的本质是让AI不那么听话也能得到正确结果 我们做了什么 —— 把原 74 个决策点里的 66 个确定性步骤从 SKILL 说明书下沉到 CLI 命令 · 状态持久化到磁盘(上下文压缩、中断、重启都不影响) 。分清 AI 与程序的边界 —— 确定性流程固化到程序,AI 只做真正需要推理的事。 AI 做(容错空间大 · 需要推理) 下沉到 CLI(零容错空间 · 要求 100%) 流程调度 · 基于 CLI stdout 的 hint 决定下一步走哪个命令(verify / iteration / done / finalize) 环境检测 · 分支切换 · AST 拉取 分析设计稿 AST 结构 · 推理布局方案 编译 · 重试计数 · 多层门禁 按 checklist 审查代码 预览截图 · diff 打分 · 回滚判定 看截图判断视觉 bug 状态持久化 · 报告生成 · CR 提交 编辑 TSX/CSS 修复 通过 stdout hint 引导 AI 下一步 · 流程调度不靠 AI 记忆 AI 漏步骤 / 假交付怎么办? —— 两层机制拦截: 每步执行前 — CLI 前置校验 state ， AI 若跳过 verify 直接跑 done CLI 立即 exit 3 + stdout 打 "必须先跑 verify" ，漏步骤根本执行不下去。 AI 声称"完成"时 — Stop Hook 最终校验交付契约(pxdiff 达标 / real_bugs=0 / MR 已建 / CDN URL 等等) 不满足则反注入指令让 AI 继续跑 ，假交付根本 stop 不了。 流程调度靠 AI · 校验靠 CLI 前置 + Stop Hook 兜底 —— 不寄希望于 AI 自觉把"AI 会不会漏"变成"CLI 会不会放行"。 具体链路实现 · 让 AI 写对 三条链路大体流程是类似的，这里就用D2Weex 为例具体介绍下。 ▐5.1 D2Weex整体架构一览 一次 D2Weex 生码任务:9 个阶段 —— 从 AST(把设计稿解析成结构化数据)分析、到生码、到编译、到三端真机预览、到视觉迭代修复、到走查闭环 —— 其中大部分步骤由 CLI 骨架自动完成 · AI 只在少数需要推理的决策点介入。 下面挑三个最能体现"让 AI 写对"这条主线的能力展开讲。 ▐5.2 代码架构 · AI 生的代码就是分层的 解决什么问题 如果 AI 生的代码是一个大文件 · UI / 数据 / 业务逻辑全混在一起 · 那接下来: 想改一处 UI · 得在一堆逻辑代码里翻 想加个数据接口 · 得动到 UI 组件 想加个业务逻辑 · UI 层也得跟着改 一次生码不难 · 难的是生完之后还能持续迭代维护。所以我们从生码那一刻就给 AI 定了架构约束:代码必须分层、必须组件化。 我们做了什么 Step 1 · 页面自动组件拆分 复杂页面不是一个大文件。AI 先分析设计稿 AST · 识别出可独立的单元(卡片、区块、模块) · 把一个页面拆成多个组件: 拆分候选评分 · AI 判断哪些单元该独立成组件 每个组件都是一个独立目录 · 可以单独预览、单独维护 页面组件 = 若干子组件的组合 Step 2 · 三层目录结构 · 数据 / UI / 业务逻辑分离 每个组件都遵循严格的三层目录: 层 内容 约束 contract/ 数据类型定义 + Mock 数据 数据契约 · Mock 不进生产包 · 构建时自动剔除 ui/ 纯 UI 组件(TSX + CSS Module) 只消费 Props · 不调服务、不访问网络、不调导航 logic/ 业务逻辑(AI 留空) 开发填充真实数据获取逻辑 为什么这么分 UI 组件是"纯"的 —— 独立可预览 · 不依赖后端 Mock 和 UI 分离 —— preview 用 mock 数据 · 上线用真实数据 · 切换零代价 逻辑层留空 · 支持并行开发 —— 业务开发写 logic/ 时 · UI 层不用动 · 两条线并行 Mock 不进生产包 —— 构建时自动剔除 · 零冗余 代码架构解决的是"AI 写得可维护" —— 通过 SKILL 规则 + rulePath 让 AI 每次生出来的代码结构统一。 同时交付门禁会check 修改的文件是否符合预期，不满足要求禁止提交不允许任务完成，打回修复。 ▐5.3 视觉修复 · 多层信号融合 解决什么问题 Diff 只有一个分数不够 —— AI 会"看走眼"。举个真实案例: 一张订单卡片 · badge 圆角被截 —— badge "3" 圆角上半被白卡背景截切了。 AI 看到的 diff 只扣了 0.5 分(被截像素面积极小) · 心理锚定"分数高应该 OK" · 自评"96% 还原"、修了错的地方(marginLeft 微调) · 真结构 bug 一路漏诊到最终交付。 单靠像素 diff 分不清"渲染抖动"和"真 bug" · 单靠 AI 看图会被缩略图和分数误导。 我们做了什么 四层信号融合 · 每层回答一个不同的问题。关键点是 L2 —— 光有 diff 分数不够 · AI 还得知道实际渲染成什么样才能对症下药。所以我们不仅从设计稿拿到期望值(Pixelator AST) · 还从真机拿到 实际渲染的 DOM 树 —— 两者双向对比 · 定位到具体是哪个字段差了(位置?尺寸?颜色?字号?) 层 回答什么 具体做法 L1 · 整图相似度 WHERE — 哪里有像素差异 像素 diff · 组件级截图 L2 · 结构对比 · 期望 vs 实际 WHAT SHOULD BE vs WHAT IS — 应该长什么样 vs 真机上实际长什么样 Pixelator AST(期望值) + weex-devtools DOM 树(真机实际值) · 逐字段对比 L3 · 像素采样验证 IS IT REALLY — 是算法瑕疵还是真 bug 局部像素抽样与颜色距离测算 L4 · Vision LLM 语义复核 IS IT ACCEPTABLE — 从语义层面判断是不是真 bug Vision LLM(Gemini 多模态) 判定:algorithm_artifact / real_bug / mixed 同时 · 交付门禁的 7 项检查中 6 项有独立交叉验证 —— CLI 检测到 badge 被截、AI 却在门禁里填"badge 完整"?必须提供反驳理由说明为什么 CLI 判断有误。没有反驳 · 直接拒绝交付。 具体表现 视觉检测准确度:60-70% → 91%+ 单个 badge 漏诊率:~50% → ~10% 交付门禁防绕过覆盖:0/7 → 6/7 ▐5.4 真机实时预览 · 让效果人人可体验 解决什么问题 Agent 自动生完了代码 · 也有了三端截图和 diff 报告 —— 但光看截图不够。 业务场景大多数带交互:点击进详情、滑动切 tab、加购弹动画、暗黑模式切换、异常态回退 —— 这些必须真机上跑才能体验。而传统链路是:研发拿到代码 → 打包 → 装机 → 打开对应页面 —— 每一步都得开发在真机边上操作。产品、运营、设计想看效果只能"喊人"。 我们做了什么 Agent 生完码 → 自动推真机 → 自动屏投到浏览器 —— 分享一个链接 · 任何人随时随地都能看到实时效果: 产品看效果:不用找开发装机 · 浏览器打开链接直接看 设计走查:不用回办公室摸真机 · 手机/电脑打开就能看 复现问题:不用截图 + 文字描述 —— 直接把浏览器链接甩过去 · "自己看" 具体表现 交互场景可验收:不只是静态截图 · 完整交互动线都能真机上体验 无门槛访问:浏览器打开链接即可 · 不需要装 debug 手淘、不需要连真机、不需要 IDE 实时反馈:Agent 改一次码 → 浏览器页面自动刷新 · 秒级看到最新效果 开发角度：对于开发可能习惯在自己手机上看到或者操作，我们在issue 评论里面也准备了预览二维码，扫码可以一键预览到手机上确认。 ▐5.5 走查即自动修复 同时这里也想说清楚一点，不是所有的视觉稿我们生码的时候都需要人工参与，实践的过程中，我们也有一些页面或者卡片AI直接完成，设计师走查一遍过的。我们目标还是追求AI自动闭环，现阶段的确还有一些问题没能彻底解决，在这前提下更好的辅助AI 快速完成修复。 解决什么问题 四层视觉门禁把准确度做到 91%+，但剩下的 5-10% 里藏着最难的问题。 实际跑下来我们发现，这些残留问题不是一种形态，而是三类完全不同的场景混在一起。机器一视同仁去修，有的修不动、有的修错方向、有的根本不该修。 实测数据也印证了这一点：AI 自修复在 3轮内 ROI 最高，3 轮以上必然要转人工——要么源头就是错的，要么是算法极限，要么是端上渲染必然差异。 三类典型场景： 场景 表现 为什么必须人介入 ① 源头问题 · 设计稿不规范 + 生码折损 设计稿有调试残留 / 图层堆叠 / 分组语义错误；生码转换时 badge 被截、元素丢失、成组方向错 AI 按错误的源结构反复修，分数原地打转。人一眼看出"应该长这样"，指一下，Agent 直接改最终代码，绕过源头问题 ② 算法极限 · 人眼看不出的假偏差 字体像素级差异、5px 内偏移、抗锯齿边缘扣分——人眼几乎看不出区别，分数已到 91%+ 改了也拿不到高分，还可能引入新 bug。人判定"这是精度问题不是 bug"，直接放行 ③ 端上必然差异 · diff 前提本身不成立 客户端行高 ≥1.2（设计稿可 =1）、三端字体 baseline 不同、mock 数据 vs 真机业务数据不一致、刘海屏安全区 设计稿 vs 真机的像素比对前提失效，AI 靠 diff 循环越修越糟。只能靠人的场景判断打破死循环——"这段文字改 1.2 倍行高"，Agent 拿到提示直接微调 走查页的价值：把"3 轮后转人工"这个动作，从"现实中不标准化的流程（设计师钉钉上反馈一些信息，然后整体给到AI），压缩成一次浏览器里拖框标注、分钟级修复。 我们做了什么 一张流程图看清整个闭环(下图 6 步 · 对应本节 3 句话:01-03 → 人的输入结构化;04 → Agent 上下文精准;05-06 → 闭环全自动): 核心 3 句话: 人的输入结构化:用户屏投手淘 · 在浏览器 走查页拖框标注(位置 + 一句问题描述) · 结果结构化写入 Agent 上下文 —— 不是自然语言 bug 单 Agent 上下文精准:标注已经指定"改哪个组件的哪个属性" · Agent 直接改 —— 不用重读全组件代码 闭环全自动:标注 → Agent rerun → 修 TSX/CSS → 回写结果 → 页面实时刷新 —— 用户在同一个页面完成全流程 · 不切工具 具体表现 主观项也能收敛:从"pxdiff 91% + Vision LLM 通过" 补齐到 "用户真机看着满意" 人机协作范式升级:从"人在 Agent 外提 bug" 到 "人的判断变成 Agent 的一个决策节点" 这就是"走查即自动修复" —— 前面绝大多数问题靠机器自动化 · 最后一公里让人的判断结构化嵌入 Agent 决策循环 · 让整体的 ROI 更高。 方法论沉淀 · 让 AI Agent 变可靠的 5 条原则 前面讲的是 D2C 场景，但这套东西不只对 D2C 有用 —— 过去半年做的过程中，我们沉淀出了 5 条可迁移的方法论 · 任何 AI Agent 工作流都能用。 方法论 1 · 分清楚哪些交给 AI · 哪些交给程序 流程编排是"每步每次必须正确"的任务 → 用代码做智能判断是"大部分时候正确就够"的任务 → 用 AI 做 如果你把两者混在一个 prompt 里 · 会发生什么?确定性被拖成概率性 · 概率性被要求确定性 · 互相拖累。 判断标准:如果一个步骤"AI 做对和做错的结果完全不同" —— 比如分支切换、状态持久化、编译门禁 —— 它就是确定性步骤必须代码化。 方法论 2 · AI 决策点最小化 不是"AI 做得越多越好" · 而是"AI 用得越少 · 效果越好"。 为什么? 假设每步 AI 遵守率 95% · 74 步全流程正确率 = 0.95^74 ≈ 2%;缩到 8 步 · 全流程正确率 = 0.95^8 ≈ 66%。这不是模型能力问题 · 是数学事实。 实践:每次想让 AI 多做一件事之前 · 先问一句"这件事能不能用代码做?"能就不该让 AI 做。 我们的 AI 决策点从 74 降到 8 · 漏步骤率从 ~30% 降到 <5% —— 同一个模型 ，只是让它少做 89% 的事。 方法论 3 · 动态数据比静态指令更有效 CLI 运行时输出的结构化数据(基于当前任务的实际检测结果) · 比 SKILL 说明书里的静态规则更能驱动 AI 行动。 对比一下: 静态指令:"请检查 badge 是否被截切" → AI 可能忽略 动态数据:"badge 截切置信度 85% · 证据:外侧像素 RGB=(255,87,34) 接近 badge 主色" → AI 必须回应 前者是建议 ， 后者是事实，事实驱动行动。 对应到实践:视觉迭代前 ， CLI 自动生成一份"诊断草表" —— 里面全是基于当前模板检测出来的具体证据 ，不是通用规则。AI 拿到这份草表 ，只能按证据回应 ，不能视而不见。 方法论 4 · 交叉验证堵住 AI 的主观绕过 AI 可以在任何自然语言字段里填任何值。唯一能验证的方式是:代码有独立的检测手段 · 填写结果与检测结果矛盾时直接拒绝。 前面的方法论解决"AI 少做事" + "做对事" · 但没法防 AI 提前宣称完成。 比如 · 交付门禁里 AI 填"badge 完整" —— 你怎么知道它是真看见 badge 完整了 · 还是随手打了个 true 让流程通过? 我们的做法:CLI 有独立的像素检测。CLI 说"badge 被截 · 置信度 85%" · AI 却填"完整"?两者矛盾 —— 必须给出书面反驳理由说明为什么 CLI 判断有误，没反驳直接拒绝交付。 同样的思路可以推广:每一条 AI 可能"随手打勾"的字段 · 都应该有一个独立于 AI 的检测程序做交叉。覆盖率越高、能"随手绕过"的空间越小。 我们把这套交叉验证的通用契约沉淀成了 7 条硬约束(内部叫 Evidence Integrity R1-R7) —— 每一条都对应过一次真实翻车 —— 但这些具体规则不是关键 · "AI 填的每一个字段都要有代码验证"这个思路才是关键。 方法论 5 · AI 决策之外要有独立看门人 AI 说"我完成了" · 不能由 AI 自己决定。要有一个运行在 AI 决策循环之外的独立校验 · 不满足就拒绝退出。 前四条方法论都是"让 AI 做对更多的事" ，但 AI 依然可能在最后一刻跳过校验直接宣称完成。这时候需要一个 AI 无法绕过的机制。 我们用了 plugin 的 Stop Hook —— 简单说 · 就是在 AI 会话即将结束的时候 ·,系统会调一个外部程序做校验:通过就放行 ,不通过就把 AI 拒回去继续工作。 Fail-open:hook 本身出错就放行(绝不让防护机制拖垮工具链) 只拦当前工作流:不影响其他 Claude Code 使用 超时自动过期:防止僵尸 hook 永远拦截 关键:这个机制不在 AI 的决策链路里。AI 说"完成了"不代表真完成 —— 得由外部的代码说了算。 5 条方法论一句话总结:把"必须每次都对"的事交给代码 · 把"大部分时候对就够"的事留给 AI · 用工程化手段交叉验证 AI 的输出。这不是让 AI 更聪明 —— 是重新划分代码和 AI 的职责边界。 未来 · 让 AI 自己走完 持续打磨：从"能用"到"好用"，稳定性和性能是长期投入 —— 拉高交付成功率 、缩短端到端耗时 、覆盖更多业务边界场景 ，让 Agent 在复杂场景下也能自己收敛 人人可用：让产品、设计、运营也能直接用 issue 触发生码并最终上线 ，而不只是研发的工具 能力标准化：让 D2C 从"独立生码链路" → 进化为"可插拔进任何项目 AI 生码流程"的能力 结尾 AI 生码不难 · 难的是让 AI 自己知道对不对。 我们没有造更聪明的 AI ，做的是三件事: 分清 AI 与程序的边界： 确定性流程固化到 CLI 里 · 概率性判断留给 AI · 各司其职 给 AI 装上眼睛：三端真机截图 + 多层信号融合(像素 diff、结构对比、Vision LLM) · AI 有了自己的"眼睛" 让 AI 自己迭代修复 :看到 diff、改码、重新验证 达标才停 不再是"生完就完" AI 从设计稿到三端真机达标 ，中间的每一步都能自己感知、自己判断、自己修 —— 这就是我们在做的事情。 团队介绍 本文作者修易，来自淘天集团-用户&内容技术团队，该团队服务于淘宝基础用户产品，是淘宝最重要的业务线之一。首页、信息流推荐、消息、搜索、我淘、用增、互动、内容等亿级用户规模产品，为我们带来大量业务/技术挑战及机会。团队在保证业务的同时，以先进的跨端框架和研发模式不断完善自己，打造最极致的体验和工程技术，保障多端设备的适配和稳定运行，并探索端智能等创新机会，通过技术高效驱动业务的良性发展。持续探索以 AI 为底座构建从需求到上线的端到端自动化与产品化能力，使亿级规模的交付更快、更稳、更可控。 ¤ 拓展阅读 ¤ 3DXR技术 | 终端技术 | 音视频技术 服务端技术 | 技术质量 | 数据算法 跳转微信打开

items.title: Community safety report and new protections for teens
items.summary:
OpenAI
October 30, 2026
Safety
Community safety report and new protections for teens
ChatGPT is one of the world’s most widely used AI products, and we have invested in building some of the industry’s most advanced systems for detecting potential harm, reviewing concerning activity, and escalating credible threats. We’re making two announcements to further our work in this area: a new Community Safeguards Report and more restrictions around firearms content for minors.
Keeping communities safe⁠ continues to be a top priority for OpenAI. Our work includes bringing imminent threats of violence to the attention of law enforcement, and we made over 200 law enforcement referrals in Q3 2026. These referrals are making a positive⁠(opens in a new window) difference⁠(opens in a new window) in disrupting violent plots, and we continue to rely on mental health and behavioral experts to help us assess difficult cases.
We recognize AI companies have a distinct role to play alongside law enforcement, family members, mental-health professionals, and policymakers, who bring critical authority, context and real-world reach. We are committed to making the most of that role by continuously strengthening our systems, sharing what we learn, and working directly with those who are best positioned to act in the real world.
OpenAI’s Community Safety Report
We are constantly strengthening the steps we take to help protect people and communities. That means building strong safeguards, and also being transparent about how well they work and what we’re doing to enhance them. We want to give people a clear picture of our approach, how our models identify and respond to harmful behavior, the risks we see in practice, and the steps we take to address them.
We’re committing to launch the Community Safety Report on violence prevention and other community safety issues, and the effectiveness of our safeguards. The report will explain how we train our systems to detect, investigate, and respond to community safety issues. We’ll share anonymized examples of how violence-related harm manifests and what we’re learning, highlight new mitigations and policy changes, and include relevant data to support these findings.
We will publish our first report in early 2027, covering the second half of 2026, with updates every six months thereafter. Our commitment is to share meaningful findings about how we identify, review, and respond to potentially harmful content.
Stronger policy boundaries for all users
Our models are trained to not give instructions that would help someone plan or carry out violence. We’re now placing additional restrictions on how ChatGPT responds to questions about past mass attacks and the people who carried them out, directing the model to provide less detailed information in those areas even if it is available from other online sources. People should be able to ask ChatGPT to help them understand these events, how victims and communities were impacted, and learn about recognizing warning signs and preventing future violence. But we’re tightening our policies to restrict reconstructions of past mass attacks, including details about the weapons and equipment used and how they were obtained, and detailed comparisons on scale of harm that could amplify an attacker’s notoriety. These limits apply regardless of a user’s age or reason for asking.
Responding to warning signs
Sometimes a request that seems ordinary on its own takes on a different meaning in light of an earlier conversation. In May, we shared how ChatGPT can use short, factual summaries⁠ of earlier warning signs to respond more carefully in a later chat. We’re building on that work so that when recent chats show warning signs of possible violence, ChatGPT will respond more conservatively when sharing information that could be misused. We’re also working to apply those stricter limits when we predict someone is under 18, even if their chats show no signs of violent intent.
We ban accounts that we determine have violated our policies on violent activity⁠. We’re also working with mental health and violence prevention experts on additional, automated ways to intervene earlier. When a conversation shows signs that someone is fixating on violence or the idea of seriously harming another person, ChatGPT will be able to automatically end the chat to interrupt that pattern in the moment. If ChatGPT ends multiple chats for that reason, we may temporarily pause the account. This is an ongoing effort and we continue to strengthen and invest in technical and practical protections, including how to recognize warning signs reliably and determine when and how to intervene.
More protections for teens
ChatGPT for Teens⁠ applies age-appropriate safeguards for users under 18, with stronger protections and additional limits to reduce exposure to sensitive content. We’re now placing further limits on weapons-related information teens can receive, even when a question appears harmless.
Our policies already prohibit helping anyone plan or carry out violence and restrict helping teens find or obtain weapons. We’re extending those protections to restrict practical information about weapons and security systems that could be misused to facilitate violence, even when there’s no sign of violent intent. Teens can still use ChatGPT to help prevent and de-escalate violence, seek support, and connect with a trusted adult.
We launched age prediction⁠ last year, which analyzes multiple signals such as behavior patterns to estimate whether a user may be under or over 18. We strengthened our age prediction system to continually assess new signals as people use ChatGPT and move teens into the under 18 experience when appropriate. Users who are incorrectly placed in the under 18 experience will always have a fast, privacy-protective way to confirm they are adults and have additional teen protections removed through Persona, our age verification partner.
Our parental controls⁠ let parents link their ChatGPT accounts to their teens and manage safety settings together. Linked accounts include safety alerts⁠ that may be sent when specially trained reviewers identify a serious self-harm concern and behaviors that may be associated with disordered eating. In July, we expanded those alerts to notify parents if their teen’s account has been deactivated for violating our usage policies on violence. We are working to introduce notifications for parents if we pause their teen’s account for repeatedly discussing violence, as detailed above.
Looking ahead
Acts of real-world violence are heartbreaking and complex, with many contributing factors. They are also a stark reminder that we must continue designing and iterating our systems to account for the inherently complicated realities of human behavior. Developing effective violence safeguards in AI systems requires solving novel problems in recognizing risk and responding appropriately, and we will continue to invest in, iterate, and share learnings on how best to implement the protections we’re pursuing. The safeguards detailed here will begin rolling out in the next few weeks and we will continue to refine them. We remain committed to mitigating risks of harm in ChatGPT, strengthening our layered protections, monitoring for misuse, enforcing our rules, and involving real-world support and interventions when situations call for it.
