items.title: Fair use benefits everyone
items.summary:
OpenAI
October 30, 2026
Company
Fair use benefits everyone
Authors, journalists, creators, academics, accessibility advocates, legal experts, librarians, economists and business leaders are voicing their support for the longstanding principle of fair use and its application to AI training.
For decades, fair use has played a critical role in driving innovation that benefits everyone. It has helped deliver important medical and scientific breakthroughs and new technologies that have made real and positive differences for countless people, including authors and journalists. The New York Times’ lawsuit, meanwhile, asks everyone to ignore a half century of legal history and progress, and toss aside the longstanding principle of fair use in their own narrow pursuit of an undeserved payday.
Experts and leaders across a wide range of fields have recognized that fair use is a win-win that benefits everyone, and have shared their perspectives with the Court in filing briefs in support of fair use.
Below you’ll find excerpts from some of those submissions, in their own words. The full filings are available on the public court docket, and you can read more about fair use and AI here.
AI Progress⁠
American Council of the Blind, Association of Research Libraries, American Library Association, Consumer Technology Association & Business Software Alliance⁠
Authors Alliance⁠
Chamber of Progress, Abundance Institute and Trevor Lawrence Jr.⁠
Computer and Communications Industry Association⁠
Ed Lee and Rebecca Tushnet⁠
Electronic Frontier Foundation⁠
Engine and Developers Alliance⁠
Foundation for American Innovation⁠
Gregory Leppert⁠
Joshua S. Gans⁠
Kevin Kelly⁠
Khosla Ventures⁠
Matthew Sag⁠
Michael Wall and Sarah Rose Siskind⁠
Mike Knoop, Daniel Lowd, Douglas Schmidt⁠
Public Knowledge⁠
Senator Rick Santorum and Representative Rick Boucher⁠
Ron Suskind and Brian L. Frye⁠
United States Government⁠
AI Progress⁠(opens in a new window)
The Court should reject Plaintiffs’ attempt to extend copyright beyond its established limits. AI training uses copyrighted works for a fundamentally different purpose, does not provide the public with substitute access to those works, and does not cause the market harm cognizable under the Copyright Act. Instead, it enables a broad array of transformative technologies that are already delivering public benefits. Copyright exists to promote creativity and progress, not to suppress lawful innovation or protect authors from competition. Settled fair use principles therefore compel the conclusion that generative AI training is fair use.
American Council of the Blind, Association of Research Libraries, American Library Association, Consumer Technology Association & Business Software Alliance⁠(opens in a new window)
This case concerns more than companies that develop large language models (LLMs). It affects medical researchers and patients, educators serving students with different learning needs, people with disabilities seeking greater independence, farmers applying agricultural knowledge, independent creators developing new forms of expression, and industry sectors from software to the law. These communities share an interest in the ability to study and learn from broad and diverse sources of knowledge, and in access to the tools that make that learning useful. Many depend on systems developed by others, including open source AI systems, rather than training models themselves. Fair use supports their ability to learn, discover, communicate, and create. Restrictions on fair use training would affect both the institutions building AI and the people using it.
Authors Alliance⁠(opens in a new window)
The market dilution theory asks copyright law to protect rightsholders against an economic phenomenon that it has never restricted before. New works can reduce the sales, visibility, or value of older works without copying their protected expression. The Copyright Act deliberately leaves that competition outside the copyright owner’s control. Amicus therefore respectfully asks the Court to hold that “market dilution,” i.e., aggregate competitive pressure from noninfringing outputs, including those that occupy the same subject matter or genre, that share unprotected characteristics, or compete for the same audience, is not cognizable market harm under 17 U.S.C. § 107(4). Rejecting the theory would preserve the distinction the Second Circuit has always maintained: copyright protects authors against substitution for their protected expression, not against the success of new expression that merely competes with it.
Chamber of Progress, Abundance Institute and Trevor Lawrence Jr.⁠(opens in a new window)
The modern creative industry’s experience with generative AI provides an excellent illustration of these principles in action, demonstrating how generative AI tools advance copyright’s central purpose to enable further human creativity. For example, musicians use generative AI to explore arrangements, develop melodies, and bring projects within reach that limited resources might otherwise foreclose. These tools support and help to effectuate the artist’s judgment, expanding the possibilities for human expression and the works available to the public.
Computer and Communications Industry Association⁠(opens in a new window)
[T]raining a generative AI model is among the most clearly transformative uses a court has been asked to evaluate. The copyrighted works are not copied to be consumed or distributed; they are analyzed to extract statistical patterns that enable a tool to generate new text or other output at the direction of a human user. Both the purpose and the character of this use are categorically different from the original purpose and character of the underlying works.
Ed Lee and Rebecca Tushnet⁠(opens in a new window)
Professors of Law
These noninfringing outputs are not substantially similar to Plaintiffs’ works but are simply in the same genre or contain similar facts. Plaintiff’s unprecedented theory of “dilution” turns copyright on its head. Genres and facts are uncopyrightable. Under the Copyright Clause, these elements are not original “writings” of any “author” and are free to copy.
Electronic Frontier Foundation⁠(opens in a new window)
Plaintiffs are asking the Court to throw that caution to the winds and rewrite copyright law to include a lawful acquisition requirement that finds no basis in statute or case law; and to tilt the fair use analysis against the developer of a general-purpose tool if that tool might be used to create potentially competing non-infringing works. The Court should reject both theories.
Engine and Developers Alliance⁠(opens in a new window)
Startups’ use of foundation models demonstrates that using copyrighted works to train an AI model is a fair use, not copyright infringement. The purpose of training a foundation model is not to reproduce the works it learns; it is to build a general-purpose tool that others can adapt to new ends. The ends startups have chosen bear no resemblance to the purposes of the works in any training dataset.
Foundation for American Innovation⁠(opens in a new window)
To the extent AI training enables the creation of new knowledge, expression, software, and other capabilities, those benefits bear on factor four’s assessment of the use’s market effects. That reasoning supports a novel application here: considering the national-security value of capabilities that enable new analysis, software, and other productive work.
Gregory Leppert⁠(opens in a new window)
Library technology expert
“[T]he primary objective of copyright is not to reward the labor of authors, but to promote the Progress of Science and useful Arts.” Libraries share this fundamental purpose of the Copyright Act. For example, the Library of Congress states its mission is to provide “access to a rich, diverse and enduring source of knowledge to inform, inspire and engage you in your intellectual and creative endeavors.” Across other institutions, the language is remarkably consistent: Harvard Library’s mission is to “engage with our communities in the creation and sharing of new knowledge,” MIT Libraries seek to “advance knowledge by providing a trusted foundation for the generation, dissemination, use, creative engagement with, and preservation of information” and the New York Public Library exists to “advance knowledge by providing free and open access to materials.” The open availability of general-purpose AI models serves and supports an important public benefit in that it enables libraries to keep pace with the preservation and accessibility of human knowledge for future generations.
Joshua S. Gans⁠(opens in a new window)
Professor of Strategic Management
Copyright supports not only the incentive to create content but also the incentive to build tools that learn from that content, and a rule that treated every displaced sale as actionable can weaken the second without reliably protecting the first.
Kevin Kelly⁠(opens in a new window)
Author
AI is a transformative technology that accelerates the creation of novel works across countless disciplines in the arts and sciences. Mr. Kelly has experience in how AI advances the field of literature. In his view, each AI model can be understood as an entirely new medium that offers authors the capability to create new texts and ideas, and to reason. A ruling for Plaintiffs on fair use would therefore grant Plaintiffs far more than the limited monopoly to their original expression Congress intended to confer. It would hinder the development of technologies capable of disseminating previously unimaginable quantities of information. It would also impede new modes of thought and the creation of new original works in both the arts and sciences. Amicus files this brief in support of Defendants’ argument that the use of copyrighted works to train large language models is a fair use under 17 U.S.C. § 107. Based on his lifelong pursuits of writing, the protections afforded to copyright owners are important to Mr. Kelly. Equally vital is preserving room for permissible uses of copyrighted material and the growth of transformative technologies. Otherwise, copyright will stifle the very creativity, innovation, and spread of knowledge it exists to encourage. The fair-use doctrine is critical to ensuring that balance.
Khosla Ventures⁠(opens in a new window)
Fair use exists precisely to prevent copyright law from being used against the innovation it was designed to advance. To fulfill copyright’s constitutional mandate “[t]o promote the Progress of Science and useful Arts,” U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 8, the Court should hold that the use of copyrighted works in training OpenAI’s large language models constitutes fair use as a matter of law.
Matthew Sag⁠(opens in a new window)
Professor of Law
On the record in this case, the defendants’ use of plaintiffs’ works for AI training is highly transformative and strongly favors a finding of fair use because under realistic conditions the outputs of defendants’ models are in no relevant way similar to the invisible intermediate copies made during the training process.
Michael Wall and Sarah Rose Siskind⁠(opens in a new window)
Musician and composer / comedian and writer
This brief offers a window into what that sentence means in practice through the work of two independent creators who rely on copyright protection and AI tools to sustain their livelihoods. Amici Sarah Rose Siskind and Michael Wall are artists who create and license original works. But they use AI to handle work surrounding the creative process and to grow their businesses in a market teeming with better-resourced competitors. For Amici, AI does not displace creativity or shortcut their creative processes. AI helps them create more, and to extend their work into new modes of expression. Amici’s experience underscores the United States’ view that AI tools “can and should help level the playing field between mainstream and independent publishers.” Siskind uses AI in every aspect of her business, from day-to-day administrative tasks to developing ideas and bringing in new clients. With AI, her noncreative work is faster and less expensive, and her creative work is better. As she tells it, “I don’t think I could run my business without AI at this point.” Similarly, AI helps Wall manage the operational demands of his music business, reduce costs, and devote more of his time to composing music. Like Siskind, he doubts that his business could survive in its current form without AI.
Mike Knoop, Daniel Lowd, Douglas Schmidt⁠(opens in a new window)
Computer Scientists
Generalization and memorization are distinct phenomena. Training on a large and varied collection enables a model to respond to prompts not encountered during training, supporting the conclusion that it learns patterns applicable to new contexts rather than simply storing source works. A trained model is not an addressable document repository and does not ordinarily retrieve identified training data as stored files. There is no address, index, or file handle by which particular training data can be requested and returned; generation instead proceeds by producing a probability distribution for the next token and selecting from it.
Public Knowledge⁠(opens in a new window)
Fair use has protected tools that help people navigate the vast collections of information the digital world has brought us, including image search and full-text book search. See Perfect 10, Inc. v. Amazon.com, Inc., 508 F.3d 1146, 1164–68 (9th Cir. 2007); Authors Guild v. Google, Inc., 804 F.3d 202, 216–17, 225 (2d Cir. 2015) (“Google Books”). It has also protected libraries’ provision of accessible digital books to readers with print disabilities. See Authors Guild, Inc. v. HathiTrust, 755 F.3d 87, 101–03 (2d Cir. 2014). And it has protected free online publication of technical standards incorporated into law, recognizing the “substantial public benefits of free and easy access to the law.” Am. Soc’y for Testing & Materials v. Public.Resource.Org, Inc., 82 F.4th 1262, 1271–72 (D.C. Cir. 2023). Fair use will be equally beneficial in ensuring that AI’s benefits accrue to the public at large, instead of being controlled by a privileged few.
Senator Rick Santorum and Representative Rick Boucher⁠(opens in a new window)
Former members of Congress
“From its beginning, the law of copyright has developed in response to significant changes in technology.” Sony Corp. of Am. v. Universal City Studios, Inc., 464 U.S. 417, 430 (1984). Consistent with that provenance, the doctrine of fair use, which was made statutory law through the Copyright Act of 1976, is meant to work in tandem with technological change, not against it. AI is the latest and the most consequential technology to which that doctrine must be applied. The use of copyrighted works to train AI models is a paradigmatic case of fair use. An AI model relies on works not to communicate their expression to the public but rather, quite differently, to derive the statistical patterns of language that allow the model to function. A ruling that AI training constitutes a fair use is vitally important to our Nation. The freedom of American scientists, companies, and entrepreneurs to train AI is of paramount economic and strategic importance.
Ron Suskind and Brian L. Frye⁠(opens in a new window)
Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist / Professor of Law
OpenAI’s use of newspaper articles to train its generative AI models didn’t harm the reasonable commercial expectations of the News Plaintiffs in any way. They commissioned and published newspaper articles with the expectation of selling consumers access to those articles. They retain and continue to exercise the exclusive right to sell consumers access to their articles. Their ability to sell consumers access to their articles wasn’t affected by OpenAI’s use of those articles to train its AI models.
United States Government⁠(opens in a new window)
In this litigation, the New York Times seeks to narrow fair-use doctrine to exclude the training of OpenAI’s large language models (LLMs). That result would be inconsistent with basic copyright law principles and severely hamper “the Progress of Science and useful Arts.” U.S. CONST. art. I, § 8, cl. 8. As discussed below, publications—including independent and start-up media, in addition to the New York Times itself—are leveraging LLMs for journalistic and other purposes. And beyond the subject matter of this litigation, LLMs are already helping researchers across fields achieve major breakthroughs. Constraining LLM development under a misunderstanding of fair use doctrine would thwart such creative and scientific progress while hindering American prosperity and economic mobility.

items.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
items.summary:
OpenAI
October 30, 2026
Company
Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
Why we’re supporting a common signal that lets website operators communicate their choices to multiple AI providers at once.
Today, we’re announcing that OpenAI will honor a common signal⁠(opens in a new window) in robots.txt, the file that lets websites express their preferences about the use of their content for foundational generative AI training. This voluntary effort makes it easier for publishers and website operators to communicate the same preference to multiple participating providers at once.
Previously, website operators would identify individual crawlers and maintain separate rules for each and every provider. Having a shared signal across multiple providers reduces that work for operators.
We aim to implement the signal in the coming months, and will share another update with details about our implementation when we do so. This new signal will not replace the controls we already provide through robots.txt. Our existing crawler controls⁠(opens in a new window), which provide web publishers flexibility and control over their pages, will continue to apply and be respected.
This draws on the ongoing work⁠(opens in a new window) of the Internet Engineering Task Force’s (IETF) AI Preferences working group. We’re joining other participants in the working group in today’s announcement of this shared signal, and believe this strengthens our continued participation in the IETF standards discussions. OpenAI will continue to adapt its practices as those conversations and the landscape continue to evolve in view of appropriate controls and fairness.
We believe this is a practical step toward an open web where people can publish and discover information, and website owners have clearer, simpler ways to communicate their choices about how their content is used. We encourage other AI providers to honor the signal.

items.title: Spec it safe: shift left and harden your specs with security requirements
items.summary: Spec-driven development (SDD) is changing how large teams build software. Instead of relying on a prompt alone, you author a specification that guides an AI coding agent through design, tasks, and implementation; a flow we abbreviate here as Specify → Plan → Execute. But most specs describe what the software should do, the features a user can see and exercise, and don’t mention how it should withstand misuse. Functional requirements are naturally self-demonstrating: if login is broken, someone notices. Security requirements are often not; an app can pass every functional check while leaving an injection or authorization flaw wide open, because nothing exercises the failure case. So when a security constraint is missing from the spec, the agent has no security-focused target to build and iterate against. It falls back on whatever the framework defaults happen to do, which may be sufficient or may leave a hole, and nothing in the spec forces the question either way.

items.title: 从 AI Friendly 架构到可复制的 AI 迁移能力 - 淘宝直播搜推在线架构升级实践
items.summary: 原创 直播技术团队 2026-10-30 10:37 浙江 如何用 AI 破解 362 万行代码的维护难题? 淘宝直播推荐系统早期为追求策略快速上线，形成了多框架、多分支并存的架构，导致工程团队面临数百万行代码的沉重维护负担。为此，团队自研了轻量级执行框架，通过统一物料承载公共能力、声明式编排表达场景差异、受约束的流程语义以及结构化执行诊断，彻底重构了应用生产方式。在此基础上，团队先通过人工迁移建立验收基线，再将经验沉淀为 Skill 引导 AI 参与复杂历史应用的迁移与验证。这一实践不仅实现了性能的平稳过渡，更证明了“AI Friendly”的核心在于为 AI 提供有限、显式且可验证的工程空间，从而将一次性迁移经验转化为可复制的自动化能力。 摘要 淘宝直播推荐应用支持直播多个核心流量场景。早期，为了让算法策略快速进入实验，算法团队直接开发和维护对应场景应用的 Java UDF、图配置及代码分支。这种方式缩短了单次试验路径，但随着维护责任逐步转交到规模更小的工程团队，历史上形成的多框架、多分支和多套诊断方式开始成为持续迭代的主要成本。 复杂度不仅来自代码规模，更来自多个版本的独立演进。同一项公共能力可能存在于不同分支和部署版本中，一次修改需要分别理解上下文、评估影响、发布和验证。即使最初源自同一份实现，各版本在长期演进后也可能形成不同的行为，难以直接合并或替换。 针对这些问题，我们逐步建立统一的应用开发与迁移方式：用可复用组件承载公共能力，用声明式编排表达场景差异（即通过配置描述组件组合、参数连接和执行关系，由框架统一解释和执行），用明确的流程语义降低理解成本，并通过结构化执行记录支持诊断与验证。在这一基础上，我们先通过人工迁移建立旧系统的行为基线和验收标准，再将迁移知识、操作步骤、工具及验收规则组织为可复用的 Skill，让 AI 参与历史应用的分析、转换和修复，并通过确定性校验工具与新旧链路对比检查迁移质量。 本文将介绍这套应用编排框架的设计取舍、三项核心机制，以及从人工迁移到 Skill 复用的演进过程，并讨论它们如何为 AI 参与工程任务提供基础。我们用 AI Friendly 描述这样一组架构属性：任务上下文可以局部理解，组件契约和依赖关系显式可见，能力可以检索与组合，生成结果能够接受工具检查。 一个仍能运行、 却难以持续维护的系统 ▐2.1 早期生产方式为何合理 淘宝直播搜推应用形成于算法策略快速发展的阶段。早期工程资源相对有限，需要支持算法团队持续开展策略实验。为了缩短策略从想法到实验的路径，算法同学直接编写 Java UDF、维护图配置并完成实验上线。 在当时的约束下，这是一种务实选择：策略设计与工程实现之间沟通链路短，独立方案和代码分支能够隔离单次变化，有限的工程资源可以优先保障业务快速试验。 问题出现在业务进入多场景长期维护阶段之后。部分实验分支和场景分支长期保留，逐渐成为独立的开发、部署和维护单元；不同场景又分别使用不同框架。早期用于缩短单次实验路径的局部最优，开始转化为跨场景维护时的整体成本。 随着维护职责从较大范围的分散承担转向规模更精简的工程团队集中承接，如何以有限的人力持续维护多场景应用，成为架构演进需要解决的重要问题。过去分散在不同参与者、代码分支和执行框架中的知识，需要逐步沉淀为可复用的组件、统一的流程和验证方法，以减少重复理解、修改与排障的成本。 不过这并不意味着早期选择错误，而是原有生产方式所依赖的组织规模、团队分工和资产生命周期已经发生变化。 从策略快速试验期到多场景长期维护期的生产方式变化 ▐2.2 复杂度不在图的数量，而在复制后的独立演进 梳理线上实际运行版本后，我们发现，同一套流程和能力被复制到不同方案与代码分支中，随后因场景需求、参数配置和兼容逻辑的变化而独立演进。因此，同名逻辑图可能已具有不同的行为，代码分支的最新提交也未必对应线上部署版本。 一次公共能力升级或故障修复，需要先确认各运行版本的行为与差异，再评估影响、修改代码，并分别完成发布和回归验证。降低维护成本，需要减少公共能力的重复实现，让必要的场景差异得到明确表达和统一验证。 ▐2.3 三类问题共同推高长期成本 第一类问题是分支副本化与多框架并存。 长期分支分别维护 Java 实现和图配置，公共能力无法沿一个主干持续演进。新场景习惯复制完整分支，而不是复用公共能力后只表达差异。多框架并存又要求维护人员在不同框架的组件模型、参数规则、执行机制和排障路径之间来回切换。 第二类问题是执行模型缺少稳定语义和统一生命周期。 自由图擅长表达节点之间的连接，却不一定能突出业务阶段、主执行路径和职责边界。串行、并行、条件执行和数据依赖混合在拓扑中，阅读者需要沿连接关系逐个查看节点及其代码，才能还原真实流程。每张图又是独立定义，请求初始化、公共校验、监控上报和资源清理等横切能力只能逐图接入。 线上接口拓扑图样例1 线上接口拓扑图样例2 如上图所示，不同业务的执行拓扑形态各异，缺少统一的阶段划分和组织方式，读者需要逐一追溯节点及其依赖关系，才能还原业务流程与执行顺序。 第三类问题是执行诊断和监控能力不足且分散。 历史应用缺少与实际执行树对应的完整节点记录。线上出现异常时，现有日志通常无法直接回答：请求执行过哪些节点、最早在哪个节点失败、异常原因是什么、耗时是否超限。不同场景还分别设计日志字段、指标和排查入口，同类问题难以复用同一套查询模板和排查经验。 三类问题叠加后，维护成本会随分支、图和场景持续增加，无法随着公共能力和历史经验的积累逐步摊薄。增加人员只能缓解局部排期，新成员仍然需要重复学习不同分支、框架和场景上下文。 因此，真正需要解决的不是某个类写得太长、某张图不够直观，而是原有应用生产方式已经无法被当前团队持续承接。 我们决定重构的不是代码， 而是生产方式 ▐3.1 为什么局部措施不够 面对历史系统，最容易想到的方案包括增加人员、局部重构、替换旧框架、补充监控工具，或者直接让 AI 分析和改写代码。这些措施都有价值，但只能改善局部问题。 AI 尤其不能直接接管一个依赖人脑解释的系统。模型可以阅读大量代码，但如果真实行为同时分散在代码分支、图配置、实验参数、动态开关和外部调用中，它首先面对的不是“如何写新代码”，而是“哪一份事实才代表线上”。如果流程和参数缺少稳定契约，AI 生成得越快，错误也可能扩散得越快。 我们最终把目标重新定义为：建立一套能够支撑多场景长期维护的统一生产方式，让公共能力能够复用，让场景差异能够显式表达，让流程具备稳定语义，让执行结果能够被统一验证。 ▐3.2 从三类痛点推导运行框架能力 新的运行框架需要同时提供三组能力。 第一，统一应用和物料模型，并声明式表达差异。稳定能力由细粒度节点承载，场景差异主要通过流程组合、节点选择、参数、条件和配置表达，减少为隔离差异而复制完整代码分支的必要性。 第二，顺序优先、显式并行，并提供统一生命周期。流程应该可以自上而下阅读；串行、并行等待和异步旁路需要显式表达；请求前置和请求结束逻辑可以集中维护，不再逐图复制。 第三，统一产生结构化执行信息，并提供标准上报扩展。日志、监控和排查工具应当消费同一份执行事实，而不是要求每个业务节点自行定义诊断字段。 除了能力本身，我们还给底座设置了三项约束：轻量、易上手、扩展优先。框架只保留统一模型和执行语义所必需的机制，成熟的配置管理和中间件能力继续复用，平台差异和业务差异通过适配层与扩展点承载。 ▐3.3 为什么选择自研 现有图执行框架各有侧重，在领域组件复用、通用图执行和运行诊断等方面提供了不同能力。结合多场景应用的长期维护需求，我们希望进一步统一应用模型、场景差异表达、流程语义、公共生命周期和结构化执行信息，并通过配套平台支持组件发现、可视化编排、版本关联和发布治理。 为此，我们选择建设由执行框架和编排管理平台组成的应用编排与运行体系：框架负责定义组件契约、执行流程和生成诊断信息；平台负责组件管理、流程编排及相关管理操作。两者围绕统一的应用模型协同，连接应用的设计、配置、执行与诊断过程。 如在现有框架上实现这些目标，仍需要建设新的核心抽象和配套平台能力，同时适配底层模型及其演进节奏。考虑到这些建设投入，我们选择自主维护这一层应用模型及配套工具，根据实际需求持续演进。 总体架构设计 这套体系由轻量执行框架与配套编排管理平台组成。它将原本散落在代码与图配置中的业务能力整理为可复用组件，并通过受约束的流程结构组织这些组件。执行框架保持与应用具体宿主平台解耦，负责流程执行、依赖协调和结构化诊断信息生成；编排管理平台负责组件发现、流程编排、版本关联和发布治理。 整体可以分为四层： 物料层：用 AtomicNode、ChainNode （组成Chain）等统一接口承载细粒度能力； 编排层：用 Plan、Stage、ExecutorGroup 描述业务流程及串并行关系； 运行时层：负责条件判断、参数传递、并发调度、超时及异常处理； 诊断与适配层：生成 ExecuteRemark 执行树，并通过扩展点接入日志、监控和宿主环境。 这种分层刻意把“稳定能力”和“场景差异”拆开：稳定能力进入物料代码，流程结构、节点依赖、条件和物料配置进入编排。公共能力可以在一个主干中持续演进，不同场景仍能通过声明式配置保持必要差异。 Emeya 总体架构与各层职责 ▐4.1 AI Friendly 不是“AI 更容易写代码” 如果把 AI Friendly 理解为“模型能够快速生成代码”，这个说法并不准确。因为代码生成效果会受到模型版本、提示词和样例数量影响，它只能说明模型能力，不足以证明架构本身适合 AI 长期参与。 我们更关注的是：面对一个真实工程任务，AI 能否只读取与任务相关的局部上下文，能否在有限且稳定的工程语法内做选择，能否通过显式契约理解数据流，生成结果能否被确定性工具检查，运行后能否留下足以定位问题的证据。 按照这个标准，AI Friendly 不是一项独立功能，而是总体设计产生的工程属性： 这里需要区分运行底座和外围控制能力。固定流程层级、统一物料、参数契约和 ExecuteRemark 属于 Emeya 核心模型；DSL、Builder、metadata、解析器和校验器是围绕这套模型建设的 AI 控制层。新体系没有替 AI 保证结果正确，它提供的是一组稳定接口，使外部工具能够理解、生成、检查和重跑。 后续三个核心设计共同支撑了新体系的 AI Friendly 特性：统一物料降低单次任务需要读取的上下文，受约束流程减少需要临场推理的结构选择，结构化执行信息为验证和修复提供证据。 核心设计一： 统一物料与声明式差异 ▐5.1 从粗粒度 UDF 转向职责稳定的物料 历史节点中，一个类可能同时完成 RPC 请求构造、远程调用、结果解析和业务处理。粗粒度节点能够快速交付单个需求，却很难被其他场景直接复用；一旦部分逻辑存在差异，最简单的处理方式往往是复制类或复制分支。 新体系将业务流程拆分为职责更清晰的物料。AtomicNode 承载独立业务计算，ChainNode 承载参数构造、服务调用和结果解析等链式能力。节点通过明确的输入、输出和配置契约参与编排，不再依赖阅读完整调用链才能知道数据从哪里来、向哪里去。 细粒度不是越小越好。节点粒度需要同时满足三个条件：职责可以被一句话说明；输入输出可以稳定声明；能力存在独立测试或跨场景复用价值。纯粹为了拆分类而制造大量无意义节点，只会把代码复杂度转移到编排层。 ▐5.2 稳定能力进入代码，场景差异进入编排 我们希望用一套代码和一个主干能够承载多个场景，但这不等于强行消灭差异。真正需要消除的是“用一套代码副本表达局部差异”的方式。 在新体系中，稳定的业务能力由节点代码承载，差异主要通过以下声明表达： 选择哪些节点； 节点按照什么顺序组合； 参数如何连接； 什么条件下执行； 超时时间多长； 并行策略是什么； 场景专属配置取什么值。 这样，公共能力升级时可以沿主干一次修改，场景差异仍保留在可阅读、可比较的编排中。新增场景也不再默认复制完整分支，而是先检索已有物料，判断能否直接复用或组合复用，只为真实能力缺口新增代码。 统一框架本身不会自动回收历史分支。主干开发约束、实验结束后的合并回收、长尾分支治理仍然需要由工程制度保证。新体系提供的是让这些治理动作可以发生的技术基础，而不是用框架替代治理责任。 从粗粒度 UDF 分支副本到细粒度物料与声明式编排 核心设计二： 受约束的流程语义与统一生命周期 ▐6.1 为什么不继续使用自由图作为主要表达 自由图的优势是表达能力强，天然适合描述复杂依赖和并发关系。但表达自由也意味着阅读方式不稳定：同一类业务流程可能被不同开发者画成完全不同的拓扑，主链路和旁路任务混在一起，阅读者需要不断沿边回溯依赖。 我们做了一个明确取舍：牺牲一部分自由图的表达上限，换取稳定的阅读范式和可评审的并行边界。开发者按业务阶段阅读流程，运行时则根据并行属性和参数依赖调度任务。顺序表达不等于所有任务串行执行，框架仍然保留并发执行能力。 流程配置按照 Plan → Stage → ExecutorGroup → Node 的层级自上而下组织。Plan、Stage 保持顺序执行；需要并发时，由 ExecutorGroup 显式标记执行方式： Plan示例 ▐6.2 参数依赖既是运行契约，也是可验证事实 节点通过显式参数契约传递数据。每个节点声明输入、输出及其类型，上游输出与下游输入通过统一的参数标识（Key）建立连接。运行时可以据此协调依赖等待，工具也可以在执行前检查输入是否有生产者、类型与配置是否一致，以及数据依赖是否与执行顺序冲突。 以一个简化示例说明：节点 A 输出resultA，节点 B 将其声明为输入，二者便建立了明确的数据依赖。如果节点 B 引用了不存在的参数，或输入类型与上游输出不匹配，工具就可以在执行前指出问题；运行时则依据依赖关系，在所需输出就绪后继续执行下游节点。 通过这种方式，参数关系从隐藏在 Map、上下文对象和方法调用中的约定，转变为可以枚举和检查的显式契约。开发者能够直接查看数据的来源与去向，AI 可以依据契约理解和生成连接关系，工具则能够对这些关系进行静态校验。 ▐6.3 把公共前后置流程变成一等能力 历史应用中，请求初始化、公共上下文准备、监控上报和资源清理往往散落在不同图中。每接入一项公共能力，都需要逐图新增和配置节点。 新体系允许定义固定的全局前置 Plan 和全局后置 Plan，业务流程执行时由框架统一拼接。公共能力可以集中维护、统一装配，不再依赖每个场景重复配置。 统一生命周期的价值不只是少写几份配置，它建立了公共治理的控制点：团队可以明确哪些逻辑必须在所有请求前执行，哪些诊断和清理动作必须在请求结束时发生。 业务 Plan 与全局前置、后置 Plan 的统一生命周期 核心设计三： 让每次执行留下结构化证据 ▐7.1 日志不是附属能力，而是执行模型的一部分 如果日志完全由业务节点自行决定，不同场景最终会形成不同的字段、格式和查询方式。即使所有节点都“有日志”，维护人员仍然无法用同一套方法还原请求执行过程。 新体系将诊断信息设计为执行模型的一部分。每次任务执行都会生成与实际任务树对应的 ExecuteRemark。Plan、Stage、ExecutorGroup、AtomicNode、Chain 和 ChainNode 等执行层级都会记录名称、状态、耗时、异常和扩展信息，最终形成一棵与真实执行过程一致的 Remark 树。 这棵树提供了一份统一原料：日志系统可以把它展开为结构化日志，监控系统可以聚合节点成功率和耗时，链路平台可以还原执行拓扑，排查工具也可以定位第一个失败节点。不同场景采用同一套模型后，查询模板和排查知识才具备复用基础。 Chain ExecuteRemark 样例 { "async": 1, "taskType": "Chain", "subRemarks": [ { "async": 0, "cost": 0, "endTime": 1788262507764957, "name": "示例参数构造", "processorName": "SelfRunTaskProcessor", "startTime": 1788262507764928, "success": 1, "taskType": "ChainNode" }, { "async": 0, "cost": 4, "endTime": 1788262507769684, "name": "示例调用器", "processorName": "SelfRunTaskProcessor", "startTime": 1788262507765016, "success": 1, "taskType": "ChainNode" }, { "async": 0, "cost": 0, "endTime": 1788262507769722, "name": "示例结果解析", "processorName": "SelfRunTaskProcessor", "startTime": 1788262507769714, "success": 1, "taskType": "ChainNode" } ] } ▐7.2 框架负责产生证据，应用负责接入技术体系 新框架不负责日志存储、指标聚合、监控大盘和告警实现，它提供两个标准处理钩子：节点或执行单元完成后，可以处理对应层级的 ExecuteRemark；接口完成后，可以处理整条请求的 ExecuteRemark。 应用通过这些出口统一接入现有日志采集、耗时统计、采样存储和监控上报。钩子的执行异常会被记录并隔离，不改变原业务执行结果，避免诊断链路反向影响主业务。 从人工迁移到 AI 迁移 新体系建立了目标生产方式，但历史应用不会因此自动迁移。真实行为仍然分散在 Java UDF、图配置和实验参数中。 迁移需要先还原旧应用事实，再按照新模型重建节点和流程，最后证明新旧链路行为等价。 我们没有从“写一个迁移 Skill”开始，而是经历了三个阶段：人工迁移建立基线、AI 迁移并打磨 Skill、直接复用 Skill 迁移新场景。 从人工迁移到 Skill 复用的三阶段演进 ▐8.1 第一阶段：人工迁移建立事实与验收基线 考虑到图结构简单、输出较为稳定、迁移和验证成本可控，我们选择主播关注页作为人工迁移到新体系的首个真实业务场景。我们人工完成旧图、Java UDF、节点职责和数据依赖的还原，识别实验配置、动态条件和公共前后置行为，再将旧逻辑映射为新体系下的物料和编排配置。 人工迁移的目标不是证明人比 AI 更可靠，而是建立三类基线：哪些旧行为必须保留，旧框架概念应当如何映射到新体系，以及什么证据可以证明迁移正确。 主播关注页迁移整体投入约20人日，留下了第一批可复用资产：旧框架到新框架的概念映射、节点拆分与参数迁移规则、典型实现和编排样例、新旧链路对比方法，以及适合交给工具处理的重复任务清单。 没有这一步，后续 AI 迁移面对的只是一组散乱代码和抽象目标，生成结果即使看起来合理，也缺少事实和验收依据。 ▐8.2 第二阶段：让 AI 迁移，同时把失败沉淀为能力 直播频道页成为第一个完整的 AI 迁移场景。我们将人工迁移形成的框架知识、迁移步骤和样例写入 Skill，让 AI 参与旧应用分析、目标拓扑设计、代码和配置生成、静态对账及差异修复。 此时的 Skill 不是一个预先设计完成的提示词，而是在真实迁移中逐步形成的工程能力。迁移暴露的错误被分成两类处理： 需要理解业务含义和历史语义的问题，补充知识、规则和样例； 可以确定性判断的问题，优先沉淀为解析器、生成器和校验脚本。 例如，AI 难以稳定还原旧图依赖，就增加图解析、血缘提取和依赖报告；复杂 Plan 手写容易出错，就使用脚本生成；生成结果难以走读，就把 Plan 反解为 Markdown；Java 参数、Spring Bean 和配置容易漂移，就增加跨产物契约对账。 每发现一种可重复错误，都不只是修复当前代码，而是判断怎样让下一次迁移更早发现、自动定位并能够重跑。Skill 因此从操作说明逐渐变成知识、规程、工具和验收标准的组合。 ▐8.3 第三阶段：直接复用 Skill 迁移新场景 在后续迁移场景中，我们不再边迁移边从头建设 Skill，而是直接执行已经沉淀的标准流程： 读取旧应用和目标接口； 还原节点、依赖与配置事实； 生成迁移任务和依赖阶段； 按拓扑迁移节点； 生成代码、Bean 和 Plan； 执行确定性校验； 根据报告修复并重跑； 由人工审核业务语义和迁移结果。 复用 Skill 后，单场景整体迁移周期缩短到约 3 天。人工工作主要收敛为驱动 AI 工具执行任务、审核迁移结果、确认新旧差异，以及决定灰度、放量和回滚。 这次变化比“AI 写了多少代码”更重要：迁移经验先从人脑进入文档，再从文档进入工具，最后由 Skill 把知识、任务、工具和验收标准组织成可重复执行的过程。 复杂历史应用如何拆解为可执行迁移任务 ▐9.1 输入不是一个代码仓，而是一组运行事实 历史应用的真实行为不只存在于 Java 代码中。一次迁移至少需要同时处理： 旧框架的图或流程配置； Java UDF 和 Spring Bean； 输入输出及共享上下文； 实验参数、动态配置和条件开关； 外部服务调用和异常处理。 如果只让 Agent 阅读仓库并直接改写，它很容易把代码引用关系误当成完整业务依赖，遗漏配置、实验和运行时注入形成的隐式行为。 因此，迁移第一步不是写代码，而是建立结构化事实基线：形成节点清单，记录节点类型、职责、输入输出、配置、外部依赖和异常策略；再从图连接、参数读写和隐式引用中生成依赖图。 ▐9.2 按依赖关系划分 Stage，而不是平均切任务 依赖图生成后，迁移任务按照拓扑划分 Stage：上游依赖先迁移，无依赖或同层节点可以并行，下游只有在前置产物通过检查后才能开始。 主 Agent 负责维护全局事实、目标拓扑、公共约束和阶段状态；规模化执行任务负责迁移边界清晰的节点；确定性脚本负责图解析、任务生成、Plan 构建、参数闭环和跨产物校验。 这种分工解决三个问题： 上下文规模：把长任务拆成边界清晰的节点任务，避免上下文持续膨胀； 并行安全：由依赖关系决定哪些任务可以并行，避免下游先于上游迁移； 结果可靠：结构、配置和契约判断交给脚本，不依赖模型每次临场推理都得到相同结果。 AI 擅长理解、转换和处理局部差异，脚本擅长稳定解析、生成和校验。迁移过程不是二选一，而是让二者分别承担适合自己的工作。 AI迁移过程 如何证明迁移前后行为等价 迁移完成不能以“代码编译通过”或“接口返回成功”为标准。搜推在线链路依赖持续变化的召回、特征和打分服务，同一个请求在相近时刻执行两次，也可能因为实时数据、实验配置、缓存或服务状态不同而得到不同结果。 因此，分别请求新旧链路并比较最终响应，无法判断差异来自迁移逻辑还是两次请求获得了不同的外部数据。前面阶段的微小差异还会沿召回、打分、重排和结果组装不断放大，只比较最终结果也难以定位最早的偏差。 因此，我们建立了三层验证。 ▐10.1 第一层：静态结构与契约校验 静态检查用于回答新应用是否结构自洽，包括：节点是否完整、Bean 实现是否一致、输入参数是否都有生产者、输出是否被正确消费、Plan 是否引用有效物料、配置类型和默认值是否一致。 这类问题可以确定性判断，应尽量在部署前由脚本发现。静态检查能够证明结构和契约闭合，但不能证明业务语义天然正确。 ▐10.2 第二层：固定外部输入，分阶段比较新旧链路 为了隔离实时外部数据变化，我们采用“录制旧链路、回放给新链路”的方式：旧链路真实调用召回和打分服务时记录请求与结果，新链路在对应调用点使用同一份数据。这样，新旧链路的关键外部输入保持一致，剩余差异才更可能来自迁移逻辑。 比较也不是只看最终响应，而是按照召回、特征处理、打分、重排和结果组装逐层进行。发现差异后，先定位第一个出现偏差的阶段，再判断它属于预期配置差异、顺序无关差异、实时字段差异，还是需要修复的逻辑错误。 录制回放验证过程 ▐10.3 第三层：预发、灰度与生产观察 Mock 可以隔离外部不确定性，但也可能掩盖真实集成问题。因此，静态检查和mock对比通过后，仍需要经过预发真实调用、分批灰度和生产观察。 灰度阶段同时观察技术和业务指标：接口成功率、RT 分布、节点异常和超时、核心业务指标和策略指标。AI 和工具可以整理证据、聚合差异并给出修复候选，但灰度放量和回滚始终由人工授权。 迁移稳定性的目标不是证明 AI 永远不会出错，而是让错误尽可能早地暴露，能够定位到责任阶段，修复后可以重跑，并且每次生产决定都有证据和责任人。 结果 ▐11.1 已迁移场景的运行表现 新体系已在部分真实场景上线接流，并使用一套代码和一个主干承载所有已迁移场景。当前记录的四个场景中，迁移后的平均 RT、P99 RT 和 P999 RT 均未出现劣化： 表中数值表示“迁移后 RT - 迁移前 RT”，负数代表耗时下降。这组结果可以支持的结论是：在已经统计的场景中，新体系没有引入可见性能劣化，部分场景的长尾 RT 有所改善。 性能改善主要来自迁移过程中重新梳理执行关系，将部分不合理的串行操作调整为并行执行，而不是新框架性能更优。 ▐11.2 迁移方式已经发生变化 三个迁移阶段的人工投入或周期呈下降趋势：主播关注页人工迁移约 20 人日，直播频道页在 AI 参与并同步建设 Skill 的阶段约 10 人日，后续复用 Skill 缩短到单场景约 3 天。 这组数字来自不同规模和复杂度的场景，不能直接当作严格效率实验。它更适合说明研发重心的变化：人工从逐项理解、设计和编码，逐渐转向业务约束补充、架构取舍、差异判断和生产授权；AI 承担批量分析、结构转换、代码及配置生成和重复修复；确定性工具承担事实解析、生成和校验。 复盘：比“让 AI 写代码” 更重要的四个判断 第一，历史系统迁移必须先建立人工事实基线。 如果不知道旧系统哪些行为必须保留、概念如何映射、什么证据代表正确，AI 只能生成“看起来合理”的代码。人工迁移不是需要尽快绕过的低效步骤，而是后续自动化的事实和验收基础。 第二，先降低系统的解释成本，再扩大 AI 的执行范围。 AI 可以读取复杂代码，但稳定交付不能建立在每次都重新理解全部历史上下文上。统一物料、显式参数、受约束流程和结构化执行信息，本质上是在把人脑中的隐式知识变成机器也能使用的工程契约。 第三，确定性问题不要长期留给模型推理。 图依赖、参数闭环、Bean 注册和 Plan 结构都可以由程序稳定判断。真实迁移中，每遇到一种可重复错误，都应该判断能否沉淀为解析器、生成器或校验器。模型负责处理语义和差异，工具负责保证重复动作的稳定性。 第四，生成、验证和生产授权必须保持职责分离。 AI 可以生成代码、归纳日志和提出修复建议，但不能同时定义通过标准并批准自己的结果。业务语义、例外判断、灰度放量和回滚仍然需要明确的人工责任。可信迁移不是追求无人参与，而是让人工判断集中在真正需要负责的环节。 结语 新架构体系的价值不只在于把一种图结构替换成另一种流程结构，也不只在于帮助 AI 更容易生成代码。它真正改变的是历史应用的生产基础：公共能力有统一物料，场景差异有显式编排，执行流程有稳定语义，每次运行有结构化证据。这些结构降低了 AI 理解、生成和验证的成本，真实迁移又把一次性经验逐步沉淀为可复用的 Skill 与工具，它们共同构成了现阶段对 AI Friendly 的支撑。 这次实践给我们的最终判断是：面对复杂历史系统，AI 迁移的起点不是更长的提示词，也不是更激进的自动生成，而是先把系统改造成可理解、可约束、可验证的形态。 工程基础决定了 AI 能够安全走多远，也为未来 AI 理解需求、完成开发提供了支撑，让生成结果更可控、交付质量更稳定。 团队介绍 本文作者凉一，来自淘天集团-直播搜推工程团队。团队聚焦直播搜索、推荐与智能交互场景，负责商品、直播及直播看点的数据与索引建设，召回、粗排、精排等在线工程链路，以及面向消费者的直播 Agent 研发，持续提升系统性能、稳定性与业务迭代效率。同时，团队探索 Agent 在直播业务中的应用，推动算法能力与业务需求高效落地，为用户提供更精准、流畅、智能的直播内容发现与消费体验。 ¤ 拓展阅读 ¤ 3DXR技术 | 终端技术 | 音视频技术 服务端技术 | 技术质量 | 数据算法 跳转微信打开

items.title: 如何用 Kimi 做出更好的 3D 作品？官方教程来啦
items.summary: 原创 Kimi K3.1 Pro 2026-10-30 11:21 天津 4 个案例，5 个技巧 在 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的发布时，我们展示了用 Kimi 做出的 3D 网页、机械零件、建筑、小游戏 Demo、以及 3A级别的游戏预告片。 如何充分释放 Kimi 的智能，在 3D 场景「物尽其用」，做出精美、可交互、有着炫酷场景和运镜的 3D 作品？ 你可能听过 Blender、Three.js、Rhino，也见过 Tripo、Meshy 生成的角色，还听说过 Unity、Unreal Engine 和 Godot 这些游戏引擎，但不知道从何下手。 今天这篇文章，并不需要让大家记住这些晦涩的概念。你不必先学会 Blender、Three.js 或 Unreal Engine，就可以用 Kimi 做出属于自己的原创 3D 作品！ 我们将详细分享 Kimi Team 的内部 3D 工作流程，并带你更好地认识 Kimi K3.1 Pro 模型、以及 Kimi 官方各种 Harness！（想直接看教程？可以跳转到「上手试试！4 个案例的具体教程」部分。） 3D 建模： 参数化建模，网格化建模 2 种方式 3D 作品的第一步，是让 Kimi 构建 3D 模型。 Kimi 等 Agents 构建 3D 模型，主要有 2 种方式。具体来说，Kimi 既可以直接编写代码构造 3D 模型， 也可以调用 3D 生成服务（比如 Tripo、Meshy、Hyper 3D），他们各自适用的场景如下： 参数化建模：适合能用尺寸、结构和规则描述的建模任务，比如产品造型、家具与机械零件、建筑等等。 网格化建模：适用于人物、动物角色、雕像、怪兽和复杂道具等精细建模。 Kimi 在直接编写代码构造 3D 模型时，还会自主选择不同工具。Blender、Unity、Unreal Engine、Godot 等工具里面的每一个按钮都可以被写成 Python 脚本。我们特意训练了 Kimi K3.1 Pro 通过 Python 脚本调用各种 3D 工具的能力，这样即使一些小众软件并不支持 MCP 协议，也可以为 Kimi 所用。 而网格化建模，目前 K3.1 Pro 等大语言模型暂时还做不太好，Tripo 等 Diffusion Model 做得更好。这些 Diffusion Model 学习过大量三维物体的形状规律，可以根据参考图中的轮廓和遮挡关系，推断立体结构。为了确保良好体验，在你发起人物、动物等更适合网络化建模的任务时，Kimi 会自己整理好提示词与参考图，并调用 Tripo 等模型工具来完成。 在不同的任务中，Kimi 会组合使用这 2 种方法以及对应的工具： 当然，Kimi 不能保证每次生成都达到完美的效果，有些时候需要多轮调整，一些小技巧可以帮你规避一些问题。在「使用技巧」部分，我们将介绍一些对应的处理方法。 构建游戏： 在游戏引擎中组合 3D 模型、设计玩法 3D 模型有了，接下来我们可以构建游戏或者游戏预告片了！ 游戏引擎负责把这些 3D 资产、玩法组织起来，让场景成为可玩的作品。比如，让角色行走、让物体发生碰撞，加上任务、积分等玩法，还可以设计运镜和镜头切换。 Kimi 可以通过编写代码、调用工具，把 3D 模型导入各类游戏引擎，搭建场景，再逐步实现玩法。对于常见的游戏引擎，比如Unreal Engine、Unity、Godot，Kimi 都进行了较好的适配。前两者适合做更加庞大的游戏项目，Godot 则适合轻量小游戏的快速开发。 以下是 Kimi 目前支持的各种3D建模以及游戏引擎插件（需要本地安装的仅在 Kimi Work支持）： 从模型到各种 Harness，如何选择？ Kimi Harness 和 模型选择 Kimi 提供了从模型到 Agent 产品等各类 AI 工具。我们应该如何选择呢？ 想快速做一个 3D 网页、简单的单件模型，可以选择 kimi.com，无需下载和安装； 想调用建模软件、用游戏引擎，做3D场景的组合、复杂游戏玩法，可以使用 Kimi Work、Kimi Code，他们可以操作 Unity、Unreal Engine 等本地软件，在本地项目上迭代和修改 想要在你现有的工作流里接入 Kimi 模型，可以选择 Kimi API。 这些入口也可以配合使用。比如，你可以先在 kimi.com 快速并行验证一些想法，再把项目交给 Kimi Code 继续开发。 3D Make：搭配专业 skills、插件、工作流 我们还在 Kimi.com、Kimi Work 里上线了 3D Make 功能，从这里进入，可以使用我们为大家准备的 3D 生成 Skills 和专业工作流，生成更精细的 3D 作品。 一般来说，你不需要先记住每个 Skill 或插件的名称，描述目标即可，Kimi 会自行调用。如果你需要指定工作流时，可以参考下表： 上手试试！4 个案例的具体教程 现在，让我们通过 4 个例子，具体看看 harness 该如何选择、如何做出更好的 3D 作品。 例子1：在 Unreal Engine 中构建一座东方天宫 适用入口：Kimi Work、Kimi Code。 相关插件：Blender、Unreal Engine、MetaHuman。 在我们 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的官方宣发视频案例中，我们使用 K3.1 Pro，通过 Unreal Engine 5.8 构建了一座东方神话天宫，主角则通过 MetaHuman 创建，以下是完整的操作过程。 如果你想尝试类似作品，可以先用生图AI，生成一个你脑海中的画面，比如，侠客在天宫中行走，黄昏的天空中升起一条巨龙： 然后把这个图片给到 Kimi，输入以下结构的 Prompt，让它构建代码、搜集素材、组合场景： 制作一个东方天宫场景。首先根据我的参考图，使用 Blender 分别构建出柱廊和巨龙。随后在 Unreal Engine 中放入这些元素，并加入体积云和开源的月球素材，并用 Nanite 渲染高精度的建筑和巨龙，用 Lumen 实现动态全局光照与反射。 我们先把代表性画面做好，再扩大场景、构建人物、增加细节，更容易保持整体风格和画面质量。 在构建完基础场景后，如果你想让自己成为游戏中的主角，可以使用 Epic Games的官方软件 Live Link Face，录制一段以自己为原型的 20秒视频，并告诉 Kimi： Live Link Face上现在有一段人物视频，请导入 MetaHuman Editor 导入人物后，你可以自行在 MetaHuman Editor 中更改人物参数，也可以让 Kimi 帮你完成： 接下来，可以继续打磨人物模型，增加服装、武器等细节。比如，给到 Kimi 服装的多视角参考图，并让它在 blender 里制作衣服，迭代到你满意为止。 相关的武器，也可以进一步用 AI 生图，再让 Kimi 用 Blender 生成： 最后，让 Kimi 对全部素材进行组装，并做出击打的特效和运镜，经过多轮不断调整布局和位置，就能得到类似这样的产物了： 这个例子中，Kimi 把程序化建模、数字角色和引擎渲染组合在了一起使用： 基准考察通过生成 CAD 代码，从多视角渲染图重建 3D 模型的能力。给 K3.1 Pro 一段文字描述、一张草图或一张参考图，它能推断出物体的形状、比例和空间关系，并将其重建为可用的 3D 模型。它对现有素材库和模型库也有更强的理解。 用 Blender 构造元素。你可以先找到每个元素的参考图（可利用 AI 生图），再让 Kimi 在 Blender 中以参考图为目标，通过程序化建模分别做出柱廊与巨龙，迭代直到对形体和细节满意。 在 Unreal Engine 中组装场景。 将建筑、巨龙和通过 MetaHuman 创建的主角放进同一个空间，调整比例、位置和镜头，让角色与巨大建筑形成尺度对比。 完成画面表现。 场景的源模型合计包含 3,600 万个三角面，Kimi 自主调用了 Nanite 处理高精度几何体的渲染，并通过 Lumen 实现动态全局光照与反射。 例子2：做一个可以打印的3D台灯 适用入口：kimi.com 的 3D Make。 相关技能：3d-printing。 你可以先找一张喜欢的台灯参考图，这里我们以小红书博主 @锦州琛哥 的建筑台灯为灵感，制做一个镂空的福建土楼台灯。 你可以同时告诉 Kimi 预期尺寸，还可以把具体需要使用的灯光、电池组件规格发给 Kimi，让它在建模的时候考虑到组件位置，留出位置和散热空间： 参考这张图，设计一盏以福建土楼为原型、可以 3D 打印拼接的桌面台灯。总高约 25 厘米，灯罩直径约 15 厘米。使用 LED 灯光组件，它的尺寸是 xxxx。请将灯罩、支撑结构和底座拆成可组装的部件，预留安装空间与走线孔。保留建模代码，并分别导出 STL 文件。 Kimi 就会自动通过 Blender、CAD 等工具构造模型；之后想让灯罩更宽、底座更稳、增加更多细节，可以继续多轮调整。 最后，在 3D 打印前，你可以让 Kimi 把文件导入切片软件，帮你检查尺寸和支撑，确定打印的可行性。最终的成品如下： 例子3：调用 Blender 纯代码生成建筑物 适用入口：Kimi Work、Kimi Code 相关技能：Blender Kimi K3.1 Pro 通过纯代码调用 Blender，就可以一句话做出一座还不错的建筑模型。当然，记得把思考强度调整到「极致」或「进阶」，这样模型才会有更多细节。 如果你想尝试类似作品，可以把建筑特征、空间需求一起告诉 Kimi： 帮我做一个类似北京 Soho 建筑物风格的模型，提供多个角度的平面剖面的展示方式，里面要有完整的室内设计，包括办公区，交通空间，体现扎哈的设计思想，可以配合合适的时间点的视觉效果，外部环境和天气、日光需要按照我的配置来变化，整体的建筑和渲染贴图要 Photo reallstic. 你可以使用一些 PBR 贴图来e nhance 整体的视觉效果。 Kimi 会在建模前，检索公开设计资料，确认建筑物的外观和内饰方案。然后调用 Blender，逐个生成模型，并拼接组合起来。 在材质和景观细节上，Kimi 还会自主检索石材、木材贴图和写实树木模型，将贴图绑定到对应材质上。 例子4：用 Tripo 和 Blender 搭建一座微缩城市 适用入口：Kimi Work 相关插件：Tripo 3D 生成、Blender 让 Kimi 调用 Tripo 生成一些精致的模型元素，也是提升 3D 作品丰富度时可以考虑的一个做法。 比如，你可以给 Kimi 一些城市参考图，并告诉他可以调用 Tripo 生成雕塑等资产： 参考这些图，制作一座微缩山城。用 Blender 脚本构建起伏地形、树林、街道和连接不同高度的台阶。用 Tripo 生成广场喷泉、雕像和特色景观资产，再导入 Blender 组装。统一比例、材质与灯光，输出一段环绕城市的展示视频，并保留工程文件。 Kimi 会自主完成以下 3 步： 用代码搭建场景。 Kimi 创建地形，沿地势铺设街道和台阶，再用规则生成、排列树木。山坡高度、道路宽度、台阶数量和树林密度，都可以设为参数，方便调整。 用 Tripo 补充特色资产。 喷泉、雕像等物体分别生成，检查外形后导入 Blender。 在 Blender 中统一效果。 调整资产的位置和比例，检查道路连接、台阶衔接与物体落地，再设置材质、灯光和镜头。 收到 Kimi 第一轮的产出结果后，你可以先确认布局，再丰富细节。 你还可以先让 Kimi 输出俯视图和街道视角，检查空间关系。满意后，再添加景观资产和运镜，保留 .blend 工程与建模脚本，方便继续扩建。 Kimi 内部的 5 个使用技巧 在做产品和官方宣发视频的时候，我们深度使用了 Kimi K3.1 Pro 和 Kimi 的各种 harness，以下是 Kimi Team 一致好用、可以帮助大家做出更好作品的 5 个 tips： ① 图胜于言，多给参考图、视频 参考图、参考视频，往往比语言描述更直观。 用于生成单个模型的图片，尽量做到主体完整、背景简单、轮廓清楚。 如果提供多个角度，要确保造型、比例和配件一致。没有合适的图片，也可以先让 Kimi 帮你整理构图要求，调用图片生成工具生成设定图，确认外形后再开始建模。机械零件则需要额外标注尺寸，比如孔径、孔距和板厚。 参考视频也很有用。除了审美风格，它能帮助你说明镜头怎样移动、场景怎样切换。 ② 让 Kimi 帮你写复杂提示词 不熟悉建模术语，可以先让 Kimi 分析参考素材，把想法整理成制作要求： 分析这张图的造型、比例、材质和灯光，帮我写一份可执行的 3D 制作提示词。看不清的部分，请列出你的推测。 检查它的理解，补充你最在意的细节，再说：「按这份提示词开始制作。」 Kimi 比我们更擅长写出具体的提示词。比如， 「白色哑光外壳、深灰关节、蓝色显示屏」，比「精致、有科技感」更容易执行。精确尺寸、模型面数和骨骼绑定等要求，还需要通过工具参数或后续操作落实。 ③ 先构建场景，再细化单个模型、调整材质和灯光 做复杂场景时，可以先让 Kimi 用方块、圆柱等简单形状搭出布局。这一步叫灰模，主要用来检查比例、位置和空间关系。 先用灰模搭建展厅，输出入口、正面和俯视三个角度。布局确认后，再加入完整模型和材质。 每一步都看看结果。模型转一圈，游戏实际玩一遍，视频看完整段运镜。发现问题时，附上截图并指出位置： 保留现在的头部和身体比例，只修正手臂与躯干粘连的部分。 已经满意的部分，也明确告诉 Kimi 保留，方便下一轮集中修改。 在外形确定后，你还可以再打磨材质和灯光，提升质感。 模型看起来「hin塑料」，可能需要调整表面粗糙度；金属显得暗淡，也可能需要更合适的环境反射。可以保持模型和镜头不变，让 Kimi 做几组灯光对比： 分别尝试柔和摄影棚光、暖色侧光和冷色轮廓光，输出预览图供我选择。 Poly Haven 提供的 HDRI 也值得尝试。它记录了周围环境的亮度和颜色，可以为场景提供照明与反射。 ④ 他山之石，用好外部资产与动效库 Poly Haven：由团队与合作艺术家提供的公共三维资产库，包含模型、材质贴图和环境光资源，适合写实场景。（这里的资产采用 CC0 许可，可免费商用、修改和再分发，不强制署名。请参照许可说明使用。） Kenney：提供成套游戏素材，包括三维模型、界面和音效，适合快速搭建风格统一的小游戏。（这里的游戏素材采用 CC0 许可，可商用，不强制署名。请参照许可说明使用。） GSAP：由 GreenSock 开发、现属于 Webflow 的 JavaScript 动画库。可以编排移动、缩放、旋转和颜色变化，也能配合 Three.js 控制模型与镜头动画。（这里的全部插件、工具集可免费用于商业项目，使用时遵循其自定义许可。请参照官方说明使用。） 搭建场景时，你可以让 Kimi 先寻找资源，把下载好的素材放进项目目录： 用这个素材包搭建森林探索场景。先列出能直接使用的资产，再补充缺少的内容，统一比例和风格。同时整理资产清单，记录来源链接、许可和署名要求。 制作展示网页时，可以指定动效库和具体效果，让 Kimi 自行匹配： 用 Three.js 和 GSAP 制作森林展示页。向下滚动时，镜头沿小路缓慢前进，经过不同区域时，介绍文字依次出现。 先完成一个小场景或一段完整动效，再逐步扩展。 你可以先检查交互是否自然、加载是否流畅，再增加内容。用得顺手的素材包和动画代码，也可以保存下来，下次继续复用。 ⑤ 让 Kimi 总结成功方法，存成 Skill 做出一个满意的作品后，可以让 Kimi 把它整理成 Skill，下次继续使用。 例如，你做好了一个「产品展示的网站」，可以让 Kimi 保存常用的材质与灯光模板、镜头设置、预览检查步骤，以及导出格式。相关脚本和参考资料，也可以一起整理进来。 把这次验证过的制作流程整理成 Skill。将产品尺寸、主色和镜头时长设为可调整项，附上检查步骤，并保留工程文件。 资产库保存素材，Skill 保存方法。 随着项目积累，你的下一次制作就能从已有的模型、模板和流程开始。 K3.1 Pro 的下一步 以上，K3.1 Pro 让我们看到了 AI 在 items.title: Bring structured and unstructured data together with Amazon Quick
items.summary:
Organizations collect data in many forms. Structured data lives in databases and spreadsheets, whereas unstructured data sits in documents, reports, and files stored across file systems. Analyzing both together typically requires switching between multiple tools, running separate queries, and manually correlating results.
Amazon Quick addresses this with a unified experience. You can connect structured data through enriched datasets and unstructured data through S3-backed knowledge bases. You can then query both through a single conversational AI agent.
In this post, you learn how to:
Connect Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) as a data source and create a knowledge base.
Build a Space that combines structured and unstructured data.
Create and configure a custom chat agent that queries across both data types.
Ask questions that span structured and unstructured sources in a single conversation.
Solution architecture
The following diagram illustrates how each component connects to deliver a unified data experience through Amazon Quick.
Figure 1: Solution architecture for combining structured and unstructured data in Amazon Quick
The architecture has three layers:
Data layer: Your data exists in two forms. Unstructured content (documents, PDFs, reports) is stored in Amazon S3 and indexed through a knowledge base. Structured data (metrics, sales figures, and operational key performance indicators) is loaded as enriched datasets with semantic descriptions that the agent uses to translate questions into SQL.
Workspace layer: A Space brings both data types together into a single workspace. The Space references your knowledge base for unstructured queries and your datasets for structured queries. It can also include dashboards, file uploads, and action connectors. This is the layer where data from different sources converges into a unified context.
Agent layer: The custom chat agent links to the Space and uses it as its knowledge source. When a user asks a question, the agent determines whether to query the knowledge base, the dataset, or both, and returns a combined response with citations. Amazon Quick also applies built-in AI guardrails, such as content safety screening, to chat interactions.
With this layered approach, you can expand the solution over time. When you add a new data source to the Space, the agent linked to that Space can use it, and responses respect the permissions of the user who asks.
Prerequisites
To follow along with this walkthrough, you need:
An Amazon Quick account with an Enterprise subscription for the user who follows this walkthrough (creating datasets requires Enterprise). For details, see Amazon Quick pricing.
An Amazon S3 bucket for your business documents. To create one, see the Amazon S3 User Guide.
Amazon Quick access to your S3 bucket, granted by an Amazon Quick administrator. In the admin console, the administrator chooses Permissions, then AWS resources, selects Amazon S3, and chooses Select S3 buckets. Selected buckets have read-only permissions by default.
Permissions to create integrations, knowledge bases, datasets, spaces, and chat agents in Amazon Quick.
Prepare your sample data
This walkthrough uses two types of data:
Unstructured documents: Upload these to your Amazon S3 bucket for the knowledge base:
AnyCompany_Business_Review.pdf
AnyCompany_Market_Analysis_Report.pdf
AnyCompany_Product_Strategy_Memo.pdf
Structured data: Download this file to your computer. You upload it directly to Amazon Quick in Step 3:
Product_Sales.csv
Step 1: Create an Amazon S3 integration
Start by connecting Amazon Quick to your S3 bucket. From the Amazon Quick console, select Knowledge in the left navigation panel.
The knowledge page shows available connector types, including Amazon Q Business, Web Crawler, Amazon S3, and third-party options like Google Drive, OneDrive, and Microsoft SharePoint.
Under Amazon S3, choose Add. In the Create S3 knowledge base dialog, on the Connect S3 bucket page, provide the following details:
Name: A descriptive name for your integration (for example, “My Data Access Integration”).
S3 bucket location: Choose Quick Suite instance account to use a bucket in the same AWS account as Amazon Quick, or Other AWS account for a bucket in a different account.
S3 bucket URL: The S3 URI of the bucket containing your data. The bucket must be in the same Region as Amazon Quick.
Choose Next.
Figure 2: Create integration dialog showing the S3 connection fields
Step 2: Create a knowledge base
After the S3 integration is created, Amazon Quick prompts you to create a knowledge base. The knowledge base indexes your S3 content for AI-powered search.
Configure the knowledge base:
Name: “Business Knowledge Base”.
Description (optional): Notes about how the knowledge base will be used.
Content: Select “Add all content” to index everything in the connected S3 bucket, or “Add specific content” to specify the S3 prefixes for the folders and files to include (prefix filters are case-sensitive).
Next: Additional settings opens optional settings for document-level access control lists (ACLs) and a metadata files folder. Decide whether to use ACLs before you create the knowledge base, because you can’t change that choice later. This walkthrough uses sample data, so the default settings are sufficient. For details, see Set up and manage Amazon S3 integration.
Choose Create. A success banner confirms the S3 integration, and the knowledge base begins indexing in the background.
Figure 3: Create knowledge base dialog with the Business Knowledge Base name and content options
Step 3: Create and enrich a dataset
A dataset is your structured data file loaded into Amazon Quick. By enriching the dataset with semantic descriptions, custom instructions, and correct data types, the AI agent can interpret your data more accurately. It can then translate natural language questions into SQL queries.
Create the dataset
From the Amazon Quick home page, navigate to Data in the left navigation.
Choose Create dataset, then select Upload file.
Select the Product_Sales.csv file you downloaded earlier and choose Open.
On the confirmation screen, review the column names and data types. Choose Next to create the dataset.
Amazon Quick ingests the file into SPICE (the in-memory calculation engine) and the dataset appears in your dataset list.
The dataset takes its name from the uploaded file, so it appears as Product_Sales.csv in your account.
Enrich the dataset
Enriching your dataset with semantic information helps the AI understand your data in business context. The agent uses this context to translate natural language questions into more accurate SQL queries. From the dataset page, choose Edit dataset to enter the data preparation view.
Transform: Fix data types
In the Transform tab, update data types for columns that were auto-detected incorrectly. For this dataset:
Change Order Date and Date Key from String to Date.
Change Customer ID from String to Integer.
Change Sales, Discount, and Profit from String to Decimal.
Change Quantity and Unit Price from String to Integer.
Figure 4: Transform view showing data type changes applied to the Product_Sales.csv dataset
Output: Add semantic context
Select the Output tab to access the dataset-level enrichment fields. Here you provide context that helps the AI understand what your data represents and how to use it.
Description: Add a dataset-level description:
“Product sales transaction data for AnyCompany, covering orders from FY2024-FY2025 across North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, and Latin America. Includes order details, customer information, product lines, and revenue metrics.”
Custom instructions: Add guidance for how the AI should query this data:
USAGE GUIDELINES:
Revenue values are in USD.
When comparing performance, group by Region (North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, Latin America).
Order Date should be used for time-based trend analysis. The fiscal year matches the calendar year.
Date Key is a numeric YYYYMMDD representation of Order Date.
Sales = Quantity x Unit Price x (1 – Discount)
COMMON USE CASES:
Regional sales performance comparison.
Product line revenue analysis.
Quarterly trend identification.
Customer segmentation by industry and segment.
TAGS: Sales, revenue, orders, regional performance, product analytics
Column descriptions: Select each column in the left panel and add a description. For example:
Order ID: “Unique identifier for each sales transaction (format: REGION-YYYY-NNNNNN)”
Region: “Geographic sales region: North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, or Latin America”
Product: “AnyCompany product name: Analytics Pro, Connect, Automate, AI Assistant, Data Catalog, or Integration Hub”
Sales: “Order revenue in USD after discount”
Segment: “Customer size segment: Enterprise, Mid-Market, or SMB”
Figure 5: Output view showing dataset details with Description and Custom instructions configured
Choose Save & publish to save your changes. The dataset summary now shows the columns with their correct data types and the descriptions you added.
Figure 6: Enriched Product_Sales.csv dataset summary showing all 16 columns, data types, and descriptions
This enriched dataset provides the structured data layer for your solution. When the agent receives a natural language question about sales data, it uses these descriptions and instructions to generate more accurate SQL queries. Combined with the knowledge base from Step 2, you now have both structured and unstructured data ready to bring together in a Space.
Step 4: Create a Space
Spaces in Amazon Quick act as unified data workspaces. A Space can hold file uploads, dashboards, knowledge bases, actions, and datasets, giving your chat agent a single location to query across data types.
From the left navigation, select Spaces and create a new Space. Name it “Business Intelligence Hub”.
Add your knowledge base and dataset to the Space:
Choose Add knowledge and select Knowledge bases from the list. Select “Business Knowledge Base” from the list.
Choose Add knowledge again and select Datasets from the list. Select “Product_Sales.csv” from the list.
The Space now shows both your knowledge base (unstructured documents) and your enriched dataset (structured sales data) linked as data sources. This is the central hub where both data types come together, giving your chat agent a single place to query across everything. Figure 7 shows the Space with both resources in the Ready state.
Figure 7: Business Intelligence Hub Space showing the Product_Sales.csv dataset and Business Knowledge Base
Step 5: Create a custom chat agent
Navigate to Chat agents in the left navigation and choose Create chat agent. Amazon Quick presents a prompt builder where you can describe your agent in natural language or choose from templates like Training Guide, Project Coordinator, and Onboarding Helper.
For this walkthrough, choose Skip to configure the agent manually.
Figure 8: Chat agent creation screen with the prompt builder and sample templates
Configure the agent persona
The configuration panel has several sections. Start with the Agent Persona:
Agent identity: “Business Intelligence Assistant”
Description: “An AI assistant that breaks down information silos by analyzing business data from your knowledge base”
For Agent Persona instructions, enter:
You are a Business Intelligence Assistant designed to help organizations break down information silos. Your primary functions are:
1. Analyze business data stored in S3
2. Retrieve relevant findings from the reports and memos in the knowledge base
3. Provide comprehensive insights that connect internal data with external trends
4. Generate clear, actionable recommendations based on data analysis
When answering questions, always cite your sources and explain how you arrived at your conclusions. Focus on delivering practical business value and highlighting patterns across different information sources.
A note appears confirming that your chat agent comes equipped with enterprise guardrails.
Figure 9: Agent persona configuration with identity and persona instructions filled in
Set communication style
Under Communication style, pick a response style preset. Options include Executive, Technical, and Creative. For a business intelligence use case, select Executive.
Link knowledge sources
Under Knowledge Sources, choose Link spaces and select the “Business Intelligence Hub” Space you created earlier. This gives the agent access to your S3 knowledge base and other data sources in that Space. When you link a Space, the agent answers from large language model (LLM) knowledge and the linked resources only.
You can also attach reference documents (PDF, TXT, HTML, MD, CSV, DOC, DOCX) directly to the agent for additional context. Amazon Quick extracts up to 100,000 characters of text from the reference documents that you upload.
Figure 10: Knowledge Sources section showing the linked Business Intelligence Hub Space
Customize the agent
Under Customization, configure:
Welcome message: “Hello! I’m your Business Intelligence Assistant. I can help you analyze your sales data and business documents and provide insights by comparing internal information with market trends. How can I help you today?”
Suggested prompts: “Summarize key insights from our reports” and “Analyze our quarterly sales performance”
Figure 11: Customization section with the welcome message and suggested prompts
Launch the agent
Choose Launch chat agent. The right panel shows a live preview of your agent with the welcome message and suggested prompts displayed.
Figure 12: Launched Business Intelligence Assistant with the welcome message and suggested prompts in the chat panel
Step 6: Query across structured and unstructured data
With the agent running, start with a question about your business results:
How did sales change by region in 2025?
For this question, the agent combines results from the Product_Sales.csv dataset with the documents in the S3 knowledge base. It returns a response with regional sales breakdowns, trends, and citations that point back to each source.
Figure 13 shows the response. Each citation marker links a figure back to its source document.
Figure 13: Chat agent response showing regional sales analysis from the dataset and the knowledge base documents
When you ask a question about structured data, the agent uses text-to-SQL to translate your natural language into a SQL query. It runs the query against the dataset and returns the results in a readable format. This means you can ask complex analytical questions without writing SQL yourself.
Next, ask about a specific document:
What are the key strategic priorities outlined in our product strategy memo?
The agent summarizes the strategic pillars, the FY2026 roadmap, and the investment requirements from the Product Strategy Memo, as shown in Figure 14.
Figure 14: Chat agent response summarizing strategic priorities from the Product Strategy Memo
Finally, ask a question that needs both data types:
How do our 2025 sales results align with the market trends identified in our analysis report?
The agent compares the trends in the Market Analysis Report with results from your sales data and cites each source, as shown in Figure 15.
Figure 15: Chat agent response comparing 2025 sales results with market trends from the Market Analysis Report
This is the core value of combining data types in a single Space. The agent can pull from structured CSV data and unstructured documents in the same response. You don’t need to know where the data lives.
Step 7: Generate artifacts and reports using natural language
The Business Intelligence Assistant can also generate formatted documents, including Microsoft PowerPoint presentations, Microsoft Excel spreadsheets, and Microsoft Word documents. Try these prompts in the chat agent:
“Create a PowerPoint presentation summarizing AnyCompany’s Q4 2025 sales performance by region, including key trends and recommendations.”
“Generate an Excel spreadsheet showing the top 10 orders by revenue with Order ID, Region, Product, and Revenue columns.”
“Create a Word document with a quarterly business review summary based on our annual review data.”
Figure 16: Chat agent confirming the request and preparing a PowerPoint outline for AnyCompany’s Q4 2025 sales performance
Figure 17: Generated eight-slide PowerPoint with a downloadable AnyCompany_FY2025_Sales_Performance.pptx file
Step 8: Share the agent
When you launch a chat agent, it remains private until you share it. After you test the agent, share it with your team:
From the left navigation, choose Chat agents.
In the Actions column for Business Intelligence Assistant, choose the menu icon, and then choose Share.
Enter the users or groups to share with, assign Owner or Viewer permissions, and then choose Share.
The agent returns permissions-aware responses, and a knowledge base is available only to its creator until you update its permissions. Make sure that the people you share the agent with also have access to the Space, the knowledge base, and the dataset. For details, see Custom chat agents.
What you accomplished
In this walkthrough, you:
Connected Amazon S3 as a data source through an integration.
Created a knowledge base that indexes unstructured business documents.
Created and enriched a Product Sales dataset for structured data queries.
Built a Space that serves as a unified data hub for your chat agent.
Configured a custom chat agent with a defined persona and linked knowledge sources.
Queried the agent across structured and unstructured data in a single conversation.
Generated a PowerPoint presentation from a chat prompt.
Shared the agent with your team.
Best practices
Use the following practices as you move from this walkthrough to your own data:
Organize your S3 data: Use clear folder structures and file naming conventions. A clear structure also makes it more straightforward to scope a knowledge base to specific S3 prefixes.
Write specific persona instructions: The more specific your instructions, the more consistent the agent responses. Include guidance on how to cite sources and handle ambiguous queries.
Use Spaces to control scope: Rather than giving an agent access to everything, create focused Spaces with only the data sources relevant to that agent’s purpose.
Start with suggested prompts: Suggested prompts help users understand what the agent can do. Choose prompts that demonstrate the agent’s range across both structured and unstructured data.
Test before sharing: Use the preview panel to test your agent with representative questions before sharing it with your team.
Security considerations
Under the AWS shared responsibility model, you are responsible for configuring access to your data, knowledge bases, and agents. Consider the following as you adapt this solution:
Grant least-privilege S3 access: Give Amazon Quick access only to the buckets that your knowledge bases need. Buckets that an administrator selects have read-only permissions by default. If you create knowledge bases through the API, you can provide a custom AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role for an individual S3 data source instead of granting account-wide S3 access.
Control document access: If documents require per-user or per-group access, enable document-level ACLs when you create the knowledge base. You can’t change this choice later.
Encrypted buckets: If your bucket uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys, follow the AWS KMS steps in the administrator setup guide.
Add only trusted content: The agent uses the documents in your knowledge base to form responses, so include only content from sources you trust.
Share selectively: Chat agents and knowledge bases are private by default. Share them only with the users and groups that need them.
Use guardrails as one layer: Amazon Quick includes built-in content safety screening, and administrators can add up to 50 blocked words or phrases. These controls help reduce risk but don’t replace your responsibility to configure access and permissions. For details, see AI guardrails in Amazon Quick.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, remove the resources you created:
Delete the chat agent from the Chat agents page.
Delete the Space from the Spaces page.
Delete the Product_Sales.csv dataset from the Datasets page.
Delete the knowledge base and S3 integration from the Knowledge page.
If you created an S3 bucket specifically for this walkthrough, empty and delete it. Deleting a bucket and its objects is permanent, so back up any data that you want to keep.
Amazon Quick user subscriptions and account fees are billed separately from these resources. For details, see Amazon Quick pricing.
Conclusion
Amazon Quick helps you bring structured and unstructured data together. In this post, you connected S3 as a knowledge base, enriched a dataset, built a Space, and created a custom chat agent. Business users can now query both data types through a single conversational interface, without needing to know where the data lives or how to write queries.
About the authors

Puneeth is a Principal Technical Account Manager at AWS. He is particularly passionate about monitoring and observability, cloud financial management, and generative AI domains. In his current role, Puneeth enjoys collaborating closely with customers, using his expertise to help them design and architect their cloud workloads for optimal scale and resilience.

Sneha is a Technical Account Manager at AWS. In her role, Sneha collaborates with enterprise customers to architect, implement, and scale cloud-based applications to meet their business goals. She is passionate about cloud computing, cloud economics, and generative AI domains.

Johana is a Solutions Architect based in Arlington, Virginia, with over three years of experience designing and implementing cloud solutions. She specializes in generative AI and analytics, and loves helping customers architect solutions with security and resilience in mind. In her spare time, she enjoys spending time with her two dogs, cat, or watching sports.

Ramon is a Principal Solutions Architect for Amazon Quick. With many years of experience building BI solutions and a background in accounting, he loves working with customers and creating solutions. When not working, he prefers to be outdoors in the ocean or up on a mountain.

items.title: ServiceNow on-behalf-of token exchange with Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
How Gen Digital built Norton Revamp’s AI-curated News Engine with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search
items.summary:
Your professional reputation now lives online first. Recruiters check LinkedIn before returning a call. Clients review your digital presence before booking a first meeting. For ambitious professionals, that shift is an opportunity: a well-crafted online voice can open doors that a résumé alone never could.
But standing out takes more than content generation. It takes real-time awareness of what’s happening right now. A professional building a reputation as a generative AI thought leader needs to react to today’s breakthroughs, not last week’s headlines. And with feeds flooded by AI-generated noise, audiences reward authenticity and timeliness more than ever.
Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore made that possible. We built Norton Revamp, a generative AI-powered professional reputation management platform. At its heart is an AI-curated News Engine, powered by AgentCore Web Search, that grounds every content suggestion, goal recommendation, and news feed item in current, cited web knowledge. The platform launched in March 2026, built by a small group of engineers.
In this post, we show you how the Gen team builds an AI-curated News Engine in Norton Revamp with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search to help customers turn ideas into engaging social media posts.
The challenge: Real-time grounding for professional content
Unlike chatbots that rely on static knowledge bases, Norton Revamp needs to understand what’s trending right now in each user’s professional domain. A cyber security expert needs today’s threat intelligence. A marketing leader needs this week’s industry shifts. Traditional approaches (custom web crawlers, third-party news APIs, static content databases) each carry trade-offs: infrastructure overhead, stale data, vendor complexity, or data egress risk.
We evaluated three alternatives before choosing AgentCore Web Search. Custom crawlers require ongoing maintenance and lag real time. Third-party news APIs added vendor contracts, API key management, and data leaving our AWS environment. Static knowledge bases were perpetually stale. AgentCore Web Search eliminated these concerns. It’s fully managed with zero infrastructure overhead, operates entirely within AWS with zero data egress, and returns cited sources with URLs and publication dates. This makes personalized, real-time news feeds viable at scale.
How AgentCore Web Search powers Norton Revamp
Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a fully managed web search capability, compliant with the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It’s available as a managed connector on the AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Our agent sends a natural-language query, and Web Search returns relevant snippets, source URLs, titles, and publication dates that the model uses to produce grounded responses.
This capability powers three core features:
AI-curated news feed
Every user gets a personalized content stream surfacing the latest articles and trending topics tied to their goal. If you’re building a reputation as a generative AI thought leader, your feed prioritizes AI breakthroughs, industry analysis, and emerging use cases, sourced in real time through AgentCore Web Search. Unlike a static RSS aggregator, the feed is a goal-aware discovery engine that refreshes with every session.
Smart content suggestions
Users receive AI-generated content ideas tailored to trending topics in their space, written in their own authentic voice, with optional AI-generated visuals. AgentCore Web Search grounds every suggestion on what’s happening today. A three-step coaching flow (Analyze, Refine, Post) walks users from initial ideas to published content on LinkedIn and X, with a feedback loop, so the AI gets sharper with every iteration.
Trend-aware goal setting
Users define a goal. The AI builds a personalized roadmap with weekly themes and milestones. AgentCore Web Search feeds real-time trend data into goal generation, so weekly themes reflect current industry movements. The system learns from the past four weeks of activity, refreshing recommendations as users grow.
Architecture and tech stack
Figure 1: Event-driven architecture of the Norton Revamp News Engine
The integration follows an event-driven architecture. When a user sets or updates their professional goal, Amazon Nova (through Amazon Bedrock) generates targeted search queries based on the goal, recent activity, and engagement patterns. The agent sends these queries to AgentCore Web Search, which returns cited results entirely within our AWS environment. Our AI Learning System ranks the results for relevance, recency, and source credibility. The ranked results then serve as grounding context for Amazon Nova Lite to generate content suggestions in the user’s authentic voice. Engagement data feeds back into query generation, making the News Engine progressively smarter.
Generative AI and machine learning stack:
Amazon Bedrock – Core generative AI engine for content generation, personalization, post analysis (batch mode), and content coaching.
Amazon Nova (Nova Lite) – Primary large language model (LLM) powering content generation, goal creation, and trend analysis.
Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Real-time web retrieval powering the News Engine, content grounding, and trend discovery through an MCP-compliant managed connector.
Stability AI – Image generation.
Claude (through Amazon Bedrock) – Additional LLM capabilities for complex reasoning tasks.
Infrastructure: React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS on the frontend. Node.js, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB (multi-table with composite key patterns), Amazon API Gateway, Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS), Amazon EventBridge, Amazon CloudFront, Amazon CloudWatch, and AWS Secrets Manager on the backend. Infrastructure managed through Terraform with blue-green deployment for zero-downtime releases.
Processing pipeline: The platform runs four pipeline stages:
Full Scan – Pull up to 1,000 historical posts, store in Amazon S3, run Amazon Bedrock batch analysis for reputation impact.
Daily Scan – Amazon EventBridge-triggered incremental analysis.
Weekly Goal Generation – Lambda generates goals considering past engagement data plus real-time trend data from AgentCore Web Search.
Content Coaching – Synchronous Amazon Bedrock calls through the Analyze, Refine, Post flow, each step grounded with AgentCore Web Search results.
Engineering with an AI-native development mindset
We embedded generative AI from day one, as both the product and the development methodology. The human-AI responsibility split was deliberate: human-owned architecture decisions, security reviews, business logic, and personalization algorithms. AI handled code generation, documentation, test scaffolding, refactoring, and UI component creation.
With Claude, we produced 10 or more design variants per concept, compressed design-to-prototype time from weeks to hours and generated 70 percent of UI code with AI. We tested five pricing models in the time previously needed for one. The gamification system went through eight iterations before launching.
The measurable impact: 3x faster feature implementation, boilerplate generation accelerated by 90 percent, documentation by 80 percent, test creation by 70 percent, and UI component generation by 65 percent. The trade-off: AI output review consumed 20–30 percent of our time.
AI helped with personalization algorithms, the DynamoDB multi-table architecture (which needed experience-based judgment), security implementation, and Amazon Bedrock batch processing optimization. The key insight: AI accelerated implementation, but humans designed how the AI Learning System should adapt to user goals. Product generative AI (Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Nova, AgentCore Web Search) and development generative AI served different purposes, and we kept them separate.
Testing, security, and quality assurance
We achieved 85 percent code coverage through automated test generation. Critical test areas included content generation quality, AgentCore Web Search result relevance and freshness validation, engagement tracking accuracy, gamification logic, and news feed relevance to user goals.
For a product carrying the Norton brand, compliance is non-negotiable. Security checks spanned static code analysis, dependency vulnerability scanning, authentication flows, user data encryption, access control logic, generative AI model output validation, and content filtering. Our security team reviewed all AI-generated recommendations: AI accelerated identification, and humans made final decisions.
The result: 99.9 percent uptime since launch with real-time monitoring of generative AI content quality and user satisfaction.
Best practices for AgentCore Web Search integration
For teams considering AgentCore Web Search for real-time grounding:
Invest in query generation – Well-structured queries yield better results than open-ended ones, so we focused on our prompt engineering there.
Cache strategically – Real-time freshness is the point, but some queries don’t need to re-execute every session. We cache results with time-to-live (TTL) values that match freshness requirements.
Build feedback loops – Track which web search results users engage with and feed that signal back into query generation. Our News Engine’s relevance improved over the first 90 days.
Validate source quality – AgentCore Web Search returns source URLs and publication dates. We built a lightweight credibility scoring layer to prioritize authoritative sources.
Conclusion
Building Norton Revamp proved that a small, generative AI-augmented team can deliver enterprise software in months. It also proved that Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore can serve as the real-time intelligence backbone for products that need to stay current with the world.
We launched a generative AI-native professional reputation management platform in months, with personalized goal setting, AI-driven content suggestions, real-time curated news feeds grounded by AgentCore Web Search, adaptive learning, gamification, and Norton-grade security. A small group of engineers achieved 99.9 percent uptime.
Generative AI doesn’t replace engineers. It amplifies them. Pairing that amplification with fully managed services like AgentCore Web Search removes entire categories of infrastructure complexity. Humans designed the vision. Generative AI through Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Nova, and AgentCore Web Search accelerated bringing it to life, grounded in real-time, cited web knowledge.
“Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore eliminates the complexity of building and maintaining our own web retrieval infrastructure. It lets our Norton Revamp News Engine deliver real-time, personalized content grounded in what’s happening in each user’s professional domain, with zero data egress and Norton-grade privacy. We went from concept to production in months, and AgentCore Web Search was a key enabler.”
To learn more about Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, visit the AgentCore documentation. Check out Norton Revamp.
About the authors

Iskander is Senior Director of AI & Innovation at Gen and Board Member of the National Cybersecurity Alliance. He has helped bring multiple products from concept to launch, protecting hundreds of millions of customers and defending against billions of cyber threats

Lei is Senior Technical Director at Gen, with nearly three decades of engineering experience and many patents to his name. He has led major cloud transformations, helping bring complex technologies into production through scalable and reliable architectures
Aditya Ravikumar
Aditya is a Senior Customer Solutions Manager and Generative AI & Machine Learning SME at Amazon Web Services (AWS). Based in San Francisco, he supports Strategic enterprise customers as a principal technical advisor, helping them navigate complex cloud transformations. His areas of expertise span software development, cloud-native databases, data analytics, and production-scale Generative AI. Aditya is passionate about partnering with customers and partners to unlock transformative business value through the innovative use of cloud and AI technologies
Kien Pham
